title: Quasi-periodic oscillations from charged-particle motion around a Kerr black hole with a current-loop magnetic field

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We study the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of a charged particle around a Kerr black hole in the electromagnetic field of an equatorial current loop. The field is treated as a test field. We apply the relativistic precession model to the three simultaneous quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) of GRO J1655–40. Neutral Kerr motion reproduces the QPO frequencies and the black-hole mass measured from the companion-star orbit, but it gives a spin lower than the value obtained from fitting the thermal x-ray spectrum. In the outer dipole approximation, the three QPO frequencies can be reproduced with a mass consistent with the companion-star measurement and a spin consistent with that inferred from fitting the thermal x-ray spectrum. At leading order, the result already depends on whether the particle orbit lies inside or outside the loop; higher multipoles introduce an additional strong dependence on the loop radius. For the sampled solutions, the fitted mass remains closest to the dynamical estimate when the particle orbit lies outside a compact loop, whereas an orbit inside the loop gives larger masses.</jats:p>

title: Versatile security analysis for twin-field quantum key distribution
On the quantum nature of strong gravity

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Belenchia
                    <jats:italic>et al</jats:italic>
                    (2018
                    <jats:italic>Phys. Rev. D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:bold>98</jats:bold>
                    126009) have analyzed a gedankenexperiment where two observers, Alice and Bob, attempt to communicate via superluminal signals using a superposition of massive particles dressed by Newtonian fields and a test particle as field detector. Quantum fluctuations in the particle motion and in the field prevent signaling or violations of quantum mechanics in this setup. We reformulate this thought experiment by considering gravitational waves (GWs) emitted by an extended quadrupolar object as a detector for Newtonian tidal fields. We find that quantum fluctuations in the GWs prevent signaling. In the Newtonian limit, rotating black holes behave as extended quadrupolar objects, as a consequence of the strong equivalence principle. It follows that consistency of the Newtonian limit of general relativity with quantum mechanics requires the quantization of gravitational radiation, even when the waves originate in strong gravity sources.
                  </jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Twin-field quantum key distribution (TF-QKD) offers a repeater-like advantage in rate–distance scaling and is a promising approach for future long-distance quantum networks. However, conventional quantum encoders are typically bulky, and phase stabilization can add considerable complexity to TF-QKD systems. To address these issues, we exploit the strong electro-optic (EO) response and low-loss waveguides of thin-film lithium-niobate (TFLN) photonic platform and demonstrate a compact, coherent dual-band TF-QKD transmitter chip that integrates EO-comb generation and quantum-signal encoding. Mutually coherent on-chip comb lines serve as channel references for fast and robust phase stabilization over an open channel. Using one such chip at each user node, we demonstrate TF-QKD over a 508 km fiber link, achieving a quantum bit error rate below 0.5% and a secure key rate that surpasses the fundamental rate–distance limit by a factor of 2.67. These results establish integrated TFLN photonics as a scalable and robust platform for miniaturizing TF-QKD transmitter optics.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study demonstrates the electrically tunable nonlinear optical (NLO) response of centrosymmetric T‐graphene quantum dots (T‐GQDs) through the application of external electrostatic fields (EEFs). Using density functional theory (DFT), we show that an applied electric field effectively breaks the inversion symmetry, resulting in a significant enhancement of the first hyperpolarizability (β
                    <jats:sub>μ</jats:sub>
                    ). The NLO response exhibits strong anisotropy, with pronounced effects along the planar directions. Notably, both T‐GQDs display a superior field induced second order NLO response at stronger fields compared to hexagonal graphene quantum dots. Field dependent changes in frontier molecular orbitals and electrostatic potential surfaces reveal substantial charge redistribution and improved charge transfer character as the origin of the enhanced NLO activity. These findings establish T‐GQDs as promising candidates for electrically controlled photonic and optoelectronic devices, providing new insights into symmetry‐breaking strategies for centrosymmetric carbon nanostructures.
                  </jats:p>

title: Möbius Quantum Computation: A New Topological Resource for Quantum Error Cancellation

affiliation.name: Museum House and Quantum Laboratory, School of Arts and Sciences, La Plata City 1900, Provincia de Buenos Aires, Argentina
International School and Institute of Astro-Physics Daniel Chalonge-Hector de Vega, CNRS, INSU-Institut National des Sciences de l’Univers, Sorbonne Université, 75014 Paris, France

abstract: <jats:p>We formulate a Möbius chain mechanism for passive cancellation of coherent quantum errors under specified symmetry and evolution conditions. Möbius Quantum Computation (MQC) is a new topological boundary framework for quantum information processing, in which non-orientable boundary conditions enter explicitly into the effective quantum-state evolution. Here, we investigate a concrete consequence within this framework: the suppression of selected coherent error contributions through Möbius chain boundary conditions. While conventional quantum error correction uses redundant logical encoding, syndrome extraction, and active recovery operations, the proposed mechanism exploits a global non-orientable boundary identification, together with a compatible transformation of the error dynamics. The Möbius identification relates propagation along the chain to a twisted counterpart. The resulting cancellation depends on how the boundary transformation acts on the relevant error generators, rather than on the identification alone. We show that coherent phase errors accumulated along the ordinary branch can act against their topologically reflected contribution and they cancel themselves. The resulting mechanism is boundary-driven and passive. We formulate the boundary condition, derive the basic cancellation relation, discuss residual errors due to imperfect symmetry, and compare the proposal with dynamical decoupling, decoherence-free subspaces, stabilizer codes, and topological quantum computation. The present results identify Möbius boundary conditions as a promising and efficient resource that may complement and optimize conventional quantum error mitigation and quantum error correction. Our quantum approach is theoretical and conceptual. Its engineering and experimental architecture deserve further investigation.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We investigate the non-equilibrium work statistics originating from a sudden quench in a bosonic Josephson junction. In particular, by employing the Holstein–Primakoff approximation, the work statistics are analytically characterized in the weak-interaction regime, where the dynamics map onto a time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator. For a junction initialized in the ground state of the pre-quench Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that the work statistics are governed by a negative binomial distribution, as occurs in fully-connected models driven across a critical point. Furthermore, we also consider initial superposition states containing quantum coherences in the energy basis. To characterize the corresponding work distributions, we employ Kirkwood–Dirac quasiprobabilities (KDQ). Even in the simplest case, when the junction is initialized in a superposition of the ground and second excited states, the KDQ distribution of work exhibits negative or complex values, reflecting non-classical features. Moreover, the coherence content of the initial state can be optimized to enhance the extractable work achieved by the sudden quench, beyond classical bounds. Finally, we propose an experimental interferometric protocol to directly measure the characteristic function of the work distribution in experimentally accessible settings.</jats:p>

title: A multi-party verifiable arbitration quantum aggregate signature scheme with information hiding function
Experimental decoherence mitigation using a weak measurement-based scheme and the duality quantum algorithm
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We experimentally demonstrate a weak measurement and measurement reversal-based scheme to ameliorate the effects of decoherence due to amplitude damping, on an NMR quantum processor. The weak measurement and measurement reversal processes require the implementation of non-unitary operations, which are typically infeasible on conventional quantum processors, where only unitary quantum operations are allowed. We employed the duality quantum algorithm (DQA) for experimentally realizing the amplitude damping channel and non-unitary quantum operations corresponding to weak measurement and measurement reversal. We experimentally validate the efficacy of the weak measurement-based decoherence mitigation scheme by showing state protection on a four-qubit system, with one qubit being designated as the ‘system qubit’, while the remaining three qubits serve as ‘ancilla qubits’. Our experimental results clearly demonstrate the success of the weak measurement-based decoherence mitigation scheme in protecting the desired state. Since the measurement process involved has trace less than unity, the scheme can be thought of as a filtration scheme, where a subset of the spins is protected while the rest of the spins can be discarded.</jats:p>

title: Quantum photonic neural networks in time
abstract: <jats:p>We introduce the architecture and timing algorithm to realize a time-bin-encoded quantum photonic neural network (QPNN): a reconfigurable nonlinear photonic circuit inspired by the brain and trained to process quantum information. Unlike the typical spatially encoded QPNN, time-encoded networks require the same number of photonic elements (e.g., phase shifters or switches) regardless of their size or depth. Here, we present a model of such a network, which is inherently robust to routing errors, and show how to include imperfections such as losses and, most notably, distinguishable photons. As an example, we train the QPNN to realize a controlled-NOT gate, based on a hypothetical ideal Kerr nonlinearity. We then extend our model to a realistic two-photon nonlinearity due to scattering from a single semiconductor quantum dot coupled to a photonic waveguide. We show that, using this realistic nonlinearity, the QPNN can be trained to act as a Bell-state analyzer which operates with a fidelity of 0.96 and at a rate only limited by losses. We further show that time gating can raise this fidelity to over 0.99, while still maintaining an efficiency exceeding 0.9. Overall, this work establishes the architecture and protocol for a time-encoded QPNN, and provides a clear path to the scaling of these networks.</jats:p>

title: Architectural sensitivity of variational quantum circuits for nonlinear time-series forecasting under NISQ noise

abstract: <jats:p>Variational quantum circuits (VQCs) have been proposed as promising models for nonlinear learning tasks in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. This study presents a hybrid classical–quantum framework for nonlinear time-series forecasting that integrates causally-filtered hidden Markov regime detection with multiple VQC architectures. Four circuit architectures are defined as an explicit [Formula: see text] factorial design that isolates circuit depth from entanglement topology (shallow: depth 1/linear; ring: depth 1/ring; deep: depth 4/linear; heavy: depth 4/ring), each with reported qubit count, parameter count and gate count, and they are evaluated under an analytic depolarizing/readout noise model. Three nonlinear classical baselines (support-vector regression, gradient boosting and a multilayer perceptron) are compared alongside a linear autoregressive (AR) baseline, and the hidden Markov model (HMM) regime feature is fit only on training data and propagated causally into the test set to remove look-ahead leakage. Across 20 Monte Carlo replicates, we find that every VQC architecture is outperformed by every classical baseline, including plain linear AR (paired [Formula: see text]-tests, all [Formula: see text]; Cohen’s [Formula: see text] up to 4.8). Within the VQC family, circuit depth — not shallowness — is associated with better performance (deep/heavy [Formula: see text] shallow/ring), while entanglement topology alone has little independent effect once depth is controlled. An ablation removing the HMM-derived feature shows it contributes negligibly to forecast accuracy in this setting. Under this confound-controlled design, we find no evidence of a forecasting advantage for the tested VQC architectures over classical linear or nonlinear baselines, which we report as a cautionary result for claims of near-term quantum advantage in forecasting.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We study circular orbits of charged particles around a Schwarzschild black hole threaded by the magnetic field of a smooth finite-width equatorial current distribution. We construct an axis-regular source, retain both algebraic circular-orbit branches, and fix the coupling sign through the distant-loop limit, in which strong positive coupling drives the inner marginally stable orbit toward the horizon. We map orbit existence, radial stability, vertical stability, and bound-orbit status for both coupling signs. For positive coupling, radially stable equatorial orbits may separate into an inner band and a detached outer band, with a radial-instability gap between them. For negative coupling, the corresponding separation is produced mainly by loss of an admissible positive-angular-momentum orbit. We also identify stable off-equatorial circular-orbit families. Convergence tests and direct integration verify the principal boundaries. A regular current source can therefore reorganize the circular-orbit structure rather than merely shift the Schwarzschild innermost stable orbit.</jats:p>

title: Quantum connectivity of quantum networks

affiliation.name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
Indian Institute of Technology Bombay

abstract: <jats:p>The practical utility of a quantum network depends on its ability to establish entanglement between arbitrary node pairs with quality sufficient to execute entanglement-enabled tasks. This capability can be assessed globally, through aggregate performance over all node pairs, as well as locally, at the level of individual nodes. Since entanglement-based connections define a functional layer above the underlying physical topology, classical connectivity measures alone are insufficient to characterize quantum networks. To enable characterization of the quantum connectivity at the level of the network (or its subnetworks), we introduce the quantum connectivity measure (QCM), which quantifies the average connection quality between pairs of network nodes. We further define two quantities derived from the QCM: The quantum-connected fraction and the quantum clustering coefficient, which capture important features of the functional connectivity of the quantum network at the level of the network and an individual node, respectively. These metrics depend on the entanglement distribution protocol as well as the network parameters, and therefore capture functional aspects of quantum connectivity beyond physical topology alone. We validate the proposed measures on random and fully connected network topologies, demonstrating, in particular, that a physically fully connected graph can become functionally disconnected for quantum tasks when the average network edge concurrence falls below a critical threshold. These metrics provide useful tools for the design, optimization, and benchmarking of future quantum networks.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Atomic defects in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (2D TMDs) endow the materials with unique physical and chemical properties, promoting their potential applications in optoelectronic devices, quantum information technology, and high-efficiency catalysis. However, precise control over defect formation and reliable atomic-scale characterization remain major challenges for translating defect functionalities into practical applications. In this review, we begin with a concise overview of typical spontaneous atomic defects in as-grown 2D TMDs. We then summarize engineering strategies for introducing artificial atomic defects, including vacuum annealing, chemical doping, particle beam irradiation, and atomic manipulation. Next, we review recent progress on the characterization of the atomic structure, electronic and magnetic properties of individual point defects, as well as defect–defect interactions in multi-defect systems, with particular emphasis on scanning probe microscopy techniques. Finally, we discuss current challenges and future opportunities in controllable defect synthesis, advanced characterization, and defect-enabled device applications in 2D TMD systems.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Quantum field theory is treated as a modern, locally Lorentz-covariant quantum field version of the classical, mechanical universe suggested by Laplace over 200 years ago. Under the assumption that there is a single universal Heisenberg state that uniquely describes all physical details of our universe, a conceptual basis is given for all fundamental notions employed in laboratory physics, precise enough that the mathematical formalism is capable of yielding its own interpretation. Stochastic features arise only in approximate models; they constitute a simplified description of high-frequency effects induced by an unmodeled environment. The Born rule for quantum measurements is derived from the definition of a quantum detector via a physically intuitive detector response principle. This permits the reduction of several key aspects of the quantum measurement problem to two specific problems in mathematical physics.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>Background/Objectives: The rapid growth of the internet and cloud-based applications has led the world to adopt cloud computing. As the number of users grow there rises some problems, virtual machine allocation and cloudlet scheduling are among them. Efficient resource allocation and scheduling are crucial for balancing the load on virtual machines, as they minimize delays and optimize performance. Method: This research work proposes a predictive mechanism using Triplet Attention and Quantum-behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO). By incorporating triplet Attention, VM allocation and load balancing are performed efficiently, and the QPSO optimizes the Scheduling. For predictive models’ performance evaluation, R2 score, MAE, and RMSE metrics are evaluated. Findings: The model achieved 96.7% R2 score and the error metrics are 0.34 MAE and 0.68 RMSE, for experimental outcomes of cloud environment load balancing score, execution time, resource utilization, energy usage, and throughput are evaluated. The experimental results show that average execution time is reduced to 6.34ms from 9.38ms (AFPA), average energy consumption is reduced to 21.18Kwh from 29.95KWh (AFPA), load balancing improved to 98.06 from 98 (AFPA) throughput is increased from 51.63 (FSAOS) to 83.33 cloudlet/ms and load balancing score improved from 98.16 (AFPA) to 98.26. Novelty: The proposed model ensembles deep learning (Triplet Attention) with optimization (QPSO), and optimizes multiple key metrics at same time, the proposed model optimizes total six key metrics where the other studies only optimize two or three metrics. This work provides a comprehensive model for VM allocation and cloudlet scheduling.

Keywords: Cloud Computing, Virtual Machine Allocation, Cloudlet Scheduling, Triplet, Quantum-behaved Particle Swarm Optimization</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We propose a Lagrangian formulation for a gravity theory in which the divergence of the energy-momentum tensor in curved spacetime does not vanish. This is accomplished by introducing an arbitrary vector field that couples with the gradient of the Ricci curvature scalar. We first derive the field equations using the Palatini variational approach. Because the connection and the metric tensor are independent in the Palatini framework, the auxiliary vector field dictates whether the manifold geometry is Weyl or Riemannian. By assuming certain physically reasonable conditions on this vector field, the resulting field equations reduce to those of Rastall gravity. Furthermore, slightly different conditions on the vector field furnish unimodular gravity. For comparison, we also employ the standard metric variational approach to obtain the field equations, demonstrating that the same models can be recovered under appropriate conditions. Our key results are the derivation of a covariant Lagrangian formulation for Rastall gravity and a new Lagrangian formulation for unimodular gravity.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>O-GlcNAcylation is the post-translational addition of an O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine moiety onto serine or threonine residues of a protein. The study of O-GlcNAcylation is a rapidly growing field and has attracted researchers from a wide range of disciplines, including cell and developmental biology, cancer, chemical biology, structural biology, and immunology. O-GlcNAcylation dynamically regulates numerous cellular processes, and its dysregulation characterizes many disease states. Within the diverse and broadly significant O-GlcNAc research landscape, this review serves as a field guide for how to manipulate and measure O-GlcNAc in experiments with cultured mammalian cells, a major model system for studying O-GlcNAcylation. We discuss best practices for pharmacological and genetic modulation of global and site-specific O-GlcNAcylation, antibody- and mass spectrometry (MS)-based detection modalities, metabolic labeling and bioorthogonal chemistry, and emerging technologies for reliable O-GlcNAc detection. Finally, we recommend standard approaches to evaluating O-GlcNAc function in cultured cells, enabling sound experimental design, accurate data interpretation, and rigorous investigation of O-GlcNAc function in myriad biological contexts.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>When multi-pulse coherent integration is used to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of underwater weak targets, it is difficult for multiple targets with different strengths to be coherently integrated at the same time. When the strength difference between targets is large, the coherent integration sidelobes of strong targets hide the coherent integration peaks of weak targets, which degrades weak target detection performance. To solve this problem, this study proposes an active sonar coherent integration method for detecting strong and weak multi-targets. The frequency-domain radon Fourier transform is proposed to correct the range migration of strong targets, and an adaptive notch filter is introduced in the spatial Doppler frequency shift domain to suppress strong target energy. Subsequently, the phase differences of the remaining weak target between pulses are compensated and coherent integration is completed, thereby effectively improving weak target signal-to-noise ratio. Parameter analysis and performance comparisons are conducted to evaluate the proposed method, and its effectiveness is verified through simulations and lake experiments. The results show that the strong target suppression capability of the proposed method is more than 3 dB higher than that of the traditional CLEAN method, and that the proposed method provides superior weak target detection performance.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>We study the convective parametric amplification of the scattered wave driven by a spatially localized broadband pump in an inhomogeneous plasma in one-dimensional geometry. Two particular cases are considered: a strongly inhomogeneous plasma, in which the three-wave interaction length is shorter than the pump localization length; and a tightly focused laser beam, in which the localization length is shorter than the detuning length due to plasma inhomogeneity. A numerical solution of a pair of coupled-wave equations shows that, in both cases, the broadband pump produces a strongly nonstationary response, with large-amplitude spikes in the scattered-wave intensity. However, the time-averaged level of scattered intensity is reproducible across simulations with different pump field realizations. It shows relatively small statistical variation when the pump bandwidth exceeds the characteristic growth rate of the instability. The pump bandwidth leads to a notable difference between the forward and backward scattering (for the same characteristic growth rate). Backward-scattering amplification is smaller, and it exhibits a stronger dependence on the pump bandwidth. Conditions for mitigating spatial amplification are discussed for stimulated Raman and Brillouin scattering.</jats:p>

title: From settlement acceleration to market integration: Europe’s post-trade challenge

affiliation.name: Euronext

abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The transition towards shorter settlement cycles, combined with renewed policy efforts to deepen European capital markets integration, has brought post-trade market infrastructure to the centre of regulatory and operational debate. In Europe, this debate unfolds against a structurally fragmented settlement landscape, characterised by multiple central securities depositories (CSDs), heterogeneous market practices, and complex crossborder workflows. While recent reforms under the Central Securities Depositories Regulation and the planned move to a shortened settlement cycle to T+1 aim to enhance settlement efficiency and resilience, they expose long-standing regulatory inconsistencies that limit scalability and predictability. This paper examines how Europe’s post-trade ecosystem is adapting to these pressures, focusing on three interrelated dimensions: settlement acceleration, infrastructure integration, and digitalisation. It analyses the role of TARGET2- Securities as a harmonising settlement layer, the emergence of policy initiatives under the Savings and Investments Union (SIU), and the potential for innovation enabled by the EU DLT Pilot Regime. Particular attention is paid to regulatory initiatives within the SIU Strategy, as well as recent central bank-led initiatives, including the European Central Bank’s Pontes and Appia projects, which seek to explore how distributed ledger technology-based processes can interoperate with existing settlement infrastructures while preserving settlement finality and the use of central bank money. By situating these developments within the operational realities of CSDs and cross-border settlement, the paper argues that Europe’s posttrade future will be shaped less by technological substitution than by the ability to embed new digital processes within a coherent, interoperable, and well-governed infrastructure framework. The analysis highlights the importance of common standards, shared settlement mechanisms, and procedural harmonisation as preconditions for both settlement acceleration and sustainable digital innovation. In this context, modernising Europe’s post-trade infrastructure and fostering a competitive, innovation-driven landscape is strategically important for strengthening capital markets integration, enhancing Europe’s global competitiveness, and ensuring that European financial markets remain resilient and fit for the future. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Infected wounds, particularly those caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), often result in dysfunctional healing and fibrotic scarring. This study investigates whether a flexible dielectric barrier discharge cold atmospheric plasma (DBD-CAP) device improves healing quality in MRSA-infected murine full-thickness wounds. Mice were treated with DBD-CAP for 2 min every 48 h, and wound tissues were assessed at days 3, 7, 14, and 21. DBD-CAP treatment significantly reduced bacterial burden and inflammatory infiltration without altering macroscopic closure kinetics. In this improved microenvironment, histological analysis revealed restored basal-restricted integrin α5 polarity and ordered Ki-67 proliferation, indicating a higher quality of re-epithelialization. DBD-CAP also resulted in early angiogenesis at day 7, followed by vascular remodeling at day 14, and led to a lower collagen I/III ratio, smaller scars, and hair regrowth by day 21. Infrared thermography confirmed absence of significant thermal elevation, and repeated exposure showed no systemic toxicity. These results suggest that resolving infection with DBD-CAP creates a favorable microenvironment associated with high-quality, anti-fibrotic tissue repair, independent of accelerated closure speed. While the current experimental design cannot isolate whether these benefits are a direct regenerative effect of the plasma or a secondary, natural healing process resulting from bacterial clearance, this study provides phenotypic evidence for plasma-based wound therapy.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With the development of inertial confinement fusion facilities, the surface cleanliness of key optical components has become increasingly important for stable system operation. Conventional cleaning methods can remove organic contaminants to some extent, but residual control, secondary contamination, and process compatibility may still be challenging in ultra‐clean optical applications. Low‐pressure plasma cleaning offers low‐residue processing and reduced risk of secondary contamination. However, the cleaning mechanism and process regularities of plasma cleaning for fused silica optical components remain insufficiently understood, and systematic optimization of process parameters is still limited. Using dibutyl phthalate (DBP) as a representative organic contaminant, this study systematically investigates the adsorption behavior of DBP on fused silica, its decomposition mechanism under low‐pressure oxygen plasma, and the effects of cleaning time and power on cleaning effectiveness, thereby providing a basis for optimizing low‐pressure plasma cleaning processes. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the physical adsorption of organic contaminants on fused silica, and white‐light interferometry was employed to characterize the surface morphology of fused silica components under different contamination states. Single‐factor and full‐factorial experiments were further conducted to evaluate the effects of cleaning time and power on contaminant removal, followed by optimization of these process parameters using response surface methodology. The results clarify the reaction pathway for DBP decomposition during low‐pressure plasma cleaning and identify reasonable cleaning parameters through process optimization, providing theoretical support and experimental data for low‐pressure plasma cleaning of ultra‐clean optical components.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>
                    David Attenborough’s authority as an environmental witness has proved unusually durable, repeatedly reaffirmed within a media culture structured by acceleration and attention scarcity. That persistence owes less to celebrity visibility, persuasive messaging or advocacy than to media temporality, specifically the broadcast natural-history documentary as a form organised by return, repetition, and institutional trust. Innis’s distinction between time- and space-biased media, McLuhan’s account of media as perceptual environments and Arendt’s separation of authority from persuasion frame
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet</jats:italic>
                    as a ‘witness statement’ that makes duration its primary communicative resource. By binding ecological change to an embodied lifetime, archival return and recurring indices, the film opposes a long horizon of judgement to the short cycles of circulation characteristic of algorithmic platform infrastructures. Climate communication often produces fatigue because the temporal preconditions for authority, including continuity, shared reference points and durable institutions, are increasingly difficult to sustain. The article contributes to climate communication research by reframing environmental authority as a media-temporal condition rather than as an effect of persuasion, celebrity visibility or audience response. Attenborough’s case is therefore less a model to replicate than a limit case in which such recognition can still be inherited.

abstract: <jats:p>This paper considers linear boundary value problems, describing the electrovortex in a hemispherical vessel. This is the flow under the influence of a magnetic field generated by an electric current passing through it. The electric current flows through the liquid metal from a central hemispherical electrode to the outer conducting hemisphere. Some similar problems were studied in prior works. Solutions to these problems were previously obtained as single series composed of elementary functions. These series exhibit power-law decay estimates for their terms. The single series for the vector potential of the flow converges especially rapidly. However, computing the velocity field requires differentiating the series for the vector potential. Differentiation leads to a substantial slowdown in convergence. In the present work, summation of the slowly converging parts of the series for the vector potential and vorticity is performed. This allowed us to accelerate the convergence of the series for the velocity and pressure gradient fields of the flow. An estimate of the decrease in terms of the form O(k2l), k < 1, on any compact subset of the computational domain was obtained, instead of the previously found estimate of the form O(l−92). The summation procedure is independent of the type of boundary conditions on the spherical parts of the boundary. The procedure admits generalization to domains of different shapes. The obtained results provide a means to prove the classicality of a solution given by its Fourier series using elementary tools, as opposed to the earlier proof based on Weyl’s lemma. The results are contextualized within the framework of the earliest studies on electrovortex flows conducted in the 1960s. The computations may prove useful both for investigating the applicability of the linear approximation and for the further theoretical analysis of the nonlinear problem.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Broadband tunability is a key pursuit for terahertz (THz) free-electron lasers, yet it is often constrained by the narrow energy acceptance of laser modulators in prebunched schemes. Here, we propose a harmonic modulation scheme to decouple this constraint. Taking the Electron Source Test Facility at Dalian as a specific case study, our simulations demonstrate that by matching the laser field to higher-order harmonic resonances of the undulator, we can obtain efficient energy modulation across a significantly wider electron energy range (40–130 MeV), surpassing the limit of 71–130 MeV imposed by the fundamental resonance. This technique facilitates continuous frequency tuning from 0.5 to 30 THz using a single modulator-radiator chain, establishing a versatile method for ultrabroadband THz generation.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD), capable of sustaining non-thermal plasmas at atmospheric pressure, shows great potential for many emerging applications. This paper presents a tutorial demonstration of fundamental plasma parameters in DBDs based on the one-dimensional fluid model with Local-Mean-Energy Approximation. The model incorporates the electron density and energy balance equations coupled with Poisson’s equation, and its accuracy has been verified by comparison with experimental results. The validated model was subsequently utilized to investigate detailed DBD characteristics, encompassing discharge current, gap voltage dynamics, charge accumulation on dielectric surfaces, Lissajous figures for power calculation, and discharge symmetry. The transition of the discharge from the symmetric single-period (SP1) to the asymmetric single-period (AP1) mode is analyzed, and the formulation for the gap voltage components is derived. This work is designed to serve as a practical guide for practitioners to computational plasma discharge simulations.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>The preference for high-fat diets has increased the risk of developing cardio-metabolic metabolic
disorders. The aim of this study was to examine the effect of Justicia carnea (JC) leaf extract on
plasma and fecal lipid profile [total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), high density lipoprotein
(HDL), low density lipoprotein (LDL)] in high-fat diet fed wistar rats. The study involved a total
of thirty wistar rats separated into six groups of five rats each. Group 1 served as control while
groups 2 to 6 were fed with high-fat diet (HFD) throughout the period of the experiment. Group 2
remained untreated, Groups 3, 4 and 5 received respectively 200mg/kg, 500mg/kg and 1000mg/kg
of JC extract. Group 6 received 10mg/kg of simvastatin. The animals were fed with the extract for
twenty-eight days and thereafter plasma and fecal samples were collected to determine the lipid
profile. Daily administration of 200mg/kg of JC caused a significant reduction in the plasma levels
of total cholesterol (TC) but significant increase in fecal total cholesterol (FTC). The higher doses
also showed a similar pattern but not significantly. Administration of 500mg/kg of JC caused
significant increase in plasma TG and HDL compared to the HFD only group. All three doses of
JC caused significant reduction in LDL. Conclusively, the results from the present study suggest
that JC could possess plasma lipid lowering property and also enhanced fecal excretion of
cholesterol. This effect could be possibly due to decreased absorption of lipids and increased fecal
excretion of lipids.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nature-inspired Superhydrophobic Surfaces (SHSs) have emerged as the multifunctional interfaces which have a significant potential in engineering, environmental and biomedical applications. In this review, the state-of-the-art in the design, fabrication, and characterization of nature inspired SHSs has been reported. This paper is focused on the fabrication of SHSs with multiple micro/nanostructures, enhancement of low-surface-energy chemistry, laser surface modification, and thin-film coating approaches for extreme water repellency. The conventional reviews have mainly classified SHSs according to materials or individual applications whereas this work proposes a structure-process-property-performance framework to link biological wetting principles with laser-enabled surface engineering and coating technologies. The role of surface chemistry and hierarchical architecture in the effect of laser wavelength, pulse duration, scanning speed, hatch spacing and scanning strategy on surface morphology and wettability is also discussed. Various performance indicators are discussed which plays a crucial role in self-cleaning, anti-icing, antifouling, antifogging, drag reduction, oil-water separation, and corrosion protection applications. Environmental concerns associated with fluorinated materials and development of fluorine-free and sustainable alternatives are also addressed in this paper.</jats:p>

title: Effect of steady magnetic field on microstructure and microhardness of laser-directed energy-deposited Ti6Al4V/TiC composite coatings
abstract: <jats:p>Coarse microstructures, reinforcement agglomeration, and non-uniform property distribution are critical issues in laser-directed energy-deposited Ti6Al4V/TiC composite coatings. To address these issues, this study adopts a steady magnetic field with gradient intensities to assist the laser-directed energy deposition process. Ti-based composite coatings were fabricated on Ti6Al4V substrates under three laser processes with different heat inputs. Macroscopic observation, microstructural characterization, and microhardness tests were performed to investigate the coupled effects of magnetic field strength and laser heat input on coating formation quality, microstructural evolution, and microhardness. A magnetic modulation coupling coefficient K was proposed to quantitatively evaluate the modulation performance. The results show that the steady magnetic field effectively improved the macroscopic forming quality of the coatings. Surface defects decreased, and the wetting angle increased monotonically with rising magnetic field strength. The magnetic field&rsquo;s modulation of microstructure and hardness was highly process-dependent. Under medium- (1,000 W, 350 mm/min, 1.2 r/min) and low-heat-input processes (800 W, 350 mm/min, 1.0 r/min), a low magnetic field of 4.07 mT yielded the optimal grain refinement and TiC dispersion uniformity. For the low-heat-input process, coating hardness first decreased slightly and then increased continuously with increasing magnetic field strength. For the medium-heat-input process, hardness increased monotonically, reaching its maximum at 12.11 mT. Under the high-heat-input process (1,200 W, 250 mm/min, 1.0 r/min), a low magnetic field aggravated microstructural coarsening, and significant strengthening was achieved only when the field strength reached 12.11 mT. The maximum coating hardness reached 1155.16 HV0.2, 50.85% higher than that of the sample without a magnetic field. The hardness evolution is governed by the combined effect of grain refinement and second-phase evolution. The proposed coupling coefficient can effectively quantify the interaction between the magnetic field and laser energy, providing a theoretical reference for optimizing steady-magnetic-field-assisted laser-directed energy deposition.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Background: Meniscal tears are a common cause of knee pain and functional limitation. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP), an autologous biological therapy containing concentrated platelets and growth factors, may promote tissue healing and reduce inflammation. This study evaluated pain relief and patient satisfaction following PRP injection in patients with symptomatic meniscal tears. Methods: A prospective clinical study was conducted in the Department of Orthopaedics, Saveetha Medical College, from June 2024 to June 2026. Twenty-five patients with clinically symptomatic and MRI-confirmed meniscal tears were included. Patients received PRP injection under aseptic precautions and were followed clinically. Pain was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), while functional improvement and patient satisfaction were evaluated during follow-up. Treatment-related adverse events were also documented. Results: The mean baseline VAS score was 7.12 ± 0.83, which decreased to 5.68 ± 0.91 at 2 weeks, 4.32 ± 1.02 at 1 month, and 2.96 ± 1.08 at 3 months (p < 0.001). At 3 months, 19 patients (76%) achieved ≥50% pain relief, including 9 patients (36%) with ≥75% improvement. Functional scores improved progressively from 58.4 ± 8.6 at baseline to 78.6 ± 7.2 at 3 months (p < 0.001). Eighteen patients (72%) reported good or excellent satisfaction. No serious complications were observed. Conclusion: PRP injection demonstrated encouraging short-term pain relief, functional improvement, and patient satisfaction in patients with symptomatic meniscal tears. PRP appears to be a safe and minimally invasive treatment option in appropriately selected patients. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are warranted.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>This study aims to benchmark next-state reconstruction of one FE-generated scalar peak-temperature sequence for Ti-6Al-4V laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED) as a methodological study, not a deployment-ready process model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A conduction-dominated 10-layer wall was simulated in ANSYS Workbench Mechanical APDL 2025 R1 with temperature-dependent properties, layer activation, a Goldak-type source and convective-radiative losses. The 823-state sequence compared LSTM, XGBoost and DNN using a common target, 20-state context, chronological split, training-only scaling, scoring convention and CPU timing; model-specific inputs are documented.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across the 803-state prediction region, XGBoost achieved RMSE = 12.36 K and MAE = 7.80 K; in the 165-state late validation interval, these rose to 24.58 K and 21.14 K. Cycle- and phase-resolved diagnostics localized the strongest degradation to late-build and rapid heating/near-peak states. XGBoost gave the best accuracy-cost compromise for this data set.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The high accuracy is strictly an intra-case interpolation result for one FE-generated sequence, not evidence of cross-condition generalization or experimental fidelity. Latent heat and thermo-fluid melt-pool flow are excluded.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The present model supports only FE-sequence reconstruction and offline algorithm screening. Practical use requires matched experiments, multi-condition training, uncertainty quantification and validation of the complete sensing-control pipeline.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The transferable protocol combines target-time splitting, training-only preprocessing, explicit context exclusion, documented model-specific features, layer/phase diagnostics and amortized latency reporting, exposing degradation hidden by global R2.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydrogen energy is known for its cleanliness, high calorific value, and its abundant sources. Global attention to sustainability has driven the need to develop a technique for hydrogen production that is not only efficient but also scalable. Steam reforming is the most widely used technique for producing hydrogen because it is relatively cheaper and yields more hydrogen than other options, such as electrolysis and partial oxidation. This review provides an overview of the steam reforming process while briefly mentioning the transition of steam reforming feedstocks from methane to oxygenates (methanol, ethanol, and glycerol). Despite being a mature and efficient process, it still suffers from coking, which deactivates catalysts. This review discusses coke-mitigation techniques ranging from promoters and supports to metals, as in bi- and multi-metal catalysts. Despite their cost-effectiveness and wide use, conventional techniques produce catalysts prone to agglomeration and nonuniform dispersion; hence, the paper highlights the shift to nonconventional techniques, which provide better control over metal dispersion and improve coke resistance and catalyst stability. Lastly, this paper discusses future research directions in steam reforming, highlighting the need for stable and active catalysts.</jats:p>

title: Needleless Electrospinning of Patterned Nanofibrous Membranes with Local Fiber Alignment and Its Evaluation by Laser Scattering
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Controlled alignment of electrospun nanofibers is typically achieved using specially designed collectors in laboratory-scale needle electrospinning systems, which limits their transfer to continuous needleless electrospinning. Here, using poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) as a model polymer, we demonstrate a simple substrate-based strategy for fabricating patterned nanofibrous membranes with localized fiber alignment directly in a needleless Nanospider™ electrospinning process. Unlike previously reported methods, geometric patterning of conductive and open regions within the collection substrate controls fiber deposition and organization, eliminating the need for customized collector electrodes while remaining compatible with existing needleless electrospinning systems. The patterned substrate locally modifies the electric-field distribution, resulting in spatially selective fiber deposition, local variations in fiber density, and preferential fiber alignment. Electric-field simulations support the experimentally observed deposition behavior and show local electric-field enhancement near conductive edges and vertices, where fiber alignment was several times higher than in the central regions of the patterned structures. In addition, a rapid, non destructive laser-scattering method is introduced for quantitative evaluation of fiber alignment. The results show consistent trends with conventional SEM-based image analysis while enabling significantly faster characterization over larger membrane areas. This approach provides a practical route toward industrial-scale production of structured nanofibrous membranes with locally tailored architecture and offers a simple method for rapid assessment of fiber alignment, with potential for future application in industrial in-line quality control.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Design documentation for old buildings has largely been lost, so the facade slope measured by terrestrial laser scanning cannot be separated into initial construction deviation, accumulated deformation and local damage. A procedure of internal geometric referencing of point clouds is proposed for assessing local deformations of brick facades without design documentation. Lines in undamaged masonry of the same facade form the reference, and the slope of the studied zones is expressed as a dimensionless localisation coefficient, a multiple of the background level. On a two-storey brick building, the background level was 2.79 mm/m against 28.32–32.01 mm/m in zones adjacent to masonry discontinuities, i.e. a coefficient of 10.1–11.5. For this object, the classification remained stable under the adopted error assumptions. The procedure helps prioritise zones for subsequent opening-up inspection.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We investigate the influence of radiation pressure on the collective dynamics of a degenerate electron–positron plasma interacting with an intense radiation flux. Assuming the Fermi energy substantially exceeds the thermal energy, we apply general covariant hydrodynamic equations to demonstrate that in a sufficiently dense plasma, radiation pressure outpaces the increase of relativistic inertia, yielding an enhanced terminal bulk Lorentz factor. Furthermore, this process is accompanied by dynamic plasma cooling.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Organic electrode materials have attracted considerable attention in sodium ion batteries in recent years, yet they still face challenges such as limited energy density, poor cycling stability, and performance degradation under extreme conditions. In this work, a new donor–acceptor (D–A) type monomer, TPA-PTO, based on pyrene-4,5,9,10-tetraone and triphenylamine units is developed, and the pTPA-PTO cathode is successfully constructed through in situ electropolymerization. The pTPA-PTO cathode could successively store Na+ and PF6–, which effectively mitigates concentration polarization and enhances structural stability. Moreover, the electropolymerization further suppresses dissolution and optimizes charge transport. Consequently, pTPA-PTO achieves a high energy density of 697.23 Wh kg–1 at 0.2 A g–1 and demonstrates excellent cycling stability over 1350 cycles. Furthermore, it exhibits long-term durability at 5 A g–1 for 10,000 cycles, with an ultralow capacity decay rate of only 0.0012% per cycle. In addition, the electrode maintains superior performance under high mass loading (7.13 mg cm–2) and across a wide temperature range (–20 to 60 °C). Finally, the pTPA-PTO||HC full cell retains 90% capacity after 2600 cycles at 3 A g–1.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Constrained transmission corridors motivate comparison of high‐temperature superconducting high‐voltage direct‐current (HTS‐HVDC) with conventional VSC‐HVDC under a common receiving‐end service and contingency requirement. This study links three questions: how transmission ratings determine installed reserve, how much additional conventional corridor capital is required for parity and what conductor procurement price permits parity. The calculation purchases complete cable, converter and cooling inventories for independent modules and evaluates lifecycle expenditure and delivered energy. A 2‐GW conventional reference is compared with 2‐, 3‐, 4‐ and 5‐GW HTS planning modules using a common converter–cost relationship. At 2.1 GW receiving‐end power and 500 km, the additional conventional capital required for parity is approximately USD 0.80 billion for equal‐2‐GW modules and USD 1.39 billion for 5‐GW HTS modules. Fewer HTS assemblies can therefore coincide with a higher cost of installed reserve. Conductor‐price thresholds depend on that architecture and the assumed additional‐corridor capital; three heat‐ingress scenarios show their thermal sensitivity. Reliability and input uncertainty qualify these conditions rather than establish commercial feasibility. The calculations use published component correlations and explicit author cost and reliability scenarios. Historical project comparisons do not validate the conventional coefficients, and conductor‐current evidence does not qualify a complete 5‐GW cable system. The outputs are architecture‐specific conditions for further engineering and project appraisal, not estimates of demonstrated avoided corridor expenditure.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Global urbanisation highlights the importance of blue–green spaces for environmental quality and human well-being. However, little attention has been paid to how community and riverside green spaces are organized across varying urban contexts. This study used a purposive case study method to firstly study the micro-scale morphology of riverside and community green spaces within a 15-min walk of the Licun River in Qingdao, China, and then the Avon River in Christchurch, New Zealand. Descriptive results showed that along the Licun River, community green space provision broadly added to the provision of riverside recreational spaces and crossings, suggesting a cumulative pattern. Along the Avon River, riverside recreational spaces and crossings made up for fewer private gardens, suggesting a potentially compensatory pattern. In broad terms, riverside green space along the Licun River focused on recreation and accessibility, whereas blue–green spaces along the Avon prioritized naturalness and historical preservation. These findings highlight the importance of considering the spatial organization and connectivity of blue–green spaces in integrated, context-sensitive urban planning.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Effective water management remains a major limitation to high-power-density proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), where excessive liquid-water accumulation restricts oxygen transport and intensifies concentration losses. This study investigates a spatially engineered hydrophilic–hydrophobic flow-field strategy for passive water management, with particular emphasis on the orientation of surface wettability relative to reactant flow. Four configurations are evaluated using a three-dimensional, non-isothermal, two-phase electrochemical model: uniform wettability, hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic (Phil → Phob), hydrophobic-to-hydrophilic (Phob → Phil), and alternating wettability. The Phob → Phil configuration exhibits the best overall performance, increasing peak power density from 1.78 to 2.21 W cm
                    <jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>
                    , corresponding to a 24.2% improvement over the reference case. Under high-load conditions, it reduces flooded cathode area from 31% to 15%, oxygen depletion from 34% to 18%, and mass-transport losses from 205 to 108 mV. Temperature non-uniformity and total exergy destruction are further reduced by approximately 42.9% and 28.4%, respectively. Moreover, 89.8% of the active area operates within ±10% of the mean current density, demonstrating substantially improved electrochemical uniformity. Capillary-pressure analysis reveals that performance is governed not simply by wettability contrast, but critically by its spatial direction along the flow path. These findings establish directional hydrophilic–hydrophobic engineering as an effective passive approach for coordinating water removal, oxygen accessibility, and membrane hydration while extending stable high-power-density PEMFC operation.

title: High-density planting as an effective strategy for early sugarcane selection
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The initial stage of sugarcane breeding involves evaluating seedlings derived from biparental or polycrosses, which are subsequently assessed through vegetative propagation. In this context, the use of high-density planting may enable evaluation of more plants per family or more families within smaller areas, thereby optimizing experimental area and resources during the early stages of the breeding program. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of sugarcane genotypes selected within families under a high-density planting (HDP) system during the initial phase of genetic improvement. Two experiments were conducted at the Sugarcane Research Center of the Federal University of Viçosa. In Experiment I, 98 half-sib families were evaluated in a randomized block design with planting densities of 0.12 m within rows and 1.40 m between rows. Families were ranked based on average values of total soluble solids (Brix) and tons of cane per hectare (TCH). The ten highest-performing and ten lowest-performing families for each trait were identified. Due to overlap between groups, 34 families were ultimately selected. In Experiment II, the two most vigorous stalks per plot from these 34 families were evaluated using an augmented block design. The results showed that family classification was more consistent between experiments for Brix than for TCH. Chi-square tests confirmed a significant association between family classification in Experiment I and individual performance in Experiment II for both characteristics. Individuals selected within superior families under an HDP system maintained their performance in subsequent evaluations, contributing to more efficient resource use and optimizing the evaluation of large populations in limited areas during the early stages of sugarcane breeding.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fine-pitch hybridisation processes are essential for
  next-generation pixel detectors and high-density microelectronic
  assemblies. Conventional bump-bonding techniques, although reliable,
  remain costly and difficult to implement for single-die
  applications.

  In this work, we present flip-chip hybridisation results combining
  Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold (ENIG) bumping with Anisotropic
  Conductive Film (ACF) bonding, both developed in-house. This method
  enables fine-pitch interconnections without requiring wafer-level
  processing.

  The feasibility of the ENIG-ACF process for functional devices was
  evaluated by hybridising functional Timepix3 ASIC and Ti-LGAD
  (Trench Isolated Low-Gain Avalanche Detector) sensors with
  55 μm pitch. The approach was then extended to test
  structures with 25 μm pitch, using aligned-particle ACFs. The
  analysis revealed that the main limitation originated from the
  mismatch between ACF thickness and bump height, underlining the
  importance of interface geometry optimisation. To address this, a
  dedicated simulation program was developed to model the isotropic
  growth of ENIG bumps and to determine the optimum bump height as a
  function of ACF thickness and pixel-matrix geometry.

  The results provide valuable guidelines for future high connection
  density assemblies and show the potential of the ENIG-ACF process as
  a scalable, low-cost alternative to conventional bump-bonding
  techniques for single-die applications.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>It has been 40 years since high-temperature superconductivity (HTSC) in cuprates was discovered. Despite initial optimism, the microscopic origin of this remarkable phenomenon remains unknown. Meanwhile, advances in experimental and computational tools are shedding new light on longstanding questions. Here, we discuss an approach that differs from the conventional view and is based on lattice effects and electron correlation. In this approach, the lattice plays a main role in creating Cooper pairs in real space, while the effect of electron correlation on Bose–Einstein condensation (BEC) contributes to HTSC.</jats:p>

title: Golden economy and agriculture – Renewable energy or digitalisation and high-tech innovation
abstract: <jats:p>Sustainable and resilient agricultural systems play a key role in global growth and development. In the context of globalisation and Industry 5.0, the concept of "golden economy" is viewed from two perspectives. On the one hand, it is linked to the development of the use of renewable sources, and on the other, it is associated with digitalisation, innovation, and artificial intelligence. This study aims to analyse how the elements of the golden economy, namely renewable energy, digitalisation, and innovation, impact agriculture and to identify the challenges facing the sector. The connections between the individual elements have been deduced. An analysis of the cost-effectiveness of golden economy and its impact on agriculture has been made. The results obtained show that new and emerging technologies and their applications in the agricultural sector have the potential to impact multiple aspects of farming, including new business models and product designs, competition, operational efficiency and accessibility.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>To study the magnetic effects on dusty plasmas, magnetic fields, |B|≥1 T, are often required. When these fields are applied to the capacitively coupled plasmas that are typically used for these systems, the uniformity of the plasma is disrupted. Past experiments have shown that the plasma will form self-organized, magnetic field-aligned structures that are referred to as “filaments.” A previous study categorized these filaments as singular “types” and their correlation with the degree of magnetization through the ion Hall parameter. This paper expands on this previous work by classifying these filaments as azimuthal modes m similar to Archimedean spirals. Under this new classification, filament transformations and mixed modes are permitted to exist. By using a convolutional neural network to quantify these modes, the m=1 mode is shown to be valuable in identifying filament transformations and mixed mode states.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>In Korean high-density housing, sunlight access and the pedestrian-level wind environment are secured through separate instruments, and the cost that raising one imposes on the other has not been quantified for a whole complex. This study measures this trade-off. The as-built layout of Helio City, Seoul, is compared with two park adjustments at constant density (P1, PL1) and four whole-site reconfigurations from an explicit rule set (S1–S4). Winter-solstice sunlight access was computed at every living-room window at a 15-min step, and pedestrian-level wind speeds were determined at z = 1.5 m with an incompressible lattice Boltzmann solver under the prevailing WNW direction, simulated deterministically rather than probabilistically. Neither park adjustment produced a measurable change in either performance. Whole-site reconfiguration raised sunlight access from 49.62% to 64.22–67.46% while adding 382 to 916 dwelling units, and it lowered the winter single-cell maximum but shifted the upper tail upward: the winter 95th percentile rose from 3.76 to 4.40–5.42 m/s and the ground area above 5 m/s from 1.14% to 2.42–7.39%. This cost depended on whether the layout accounted for the prevailing wind: S3 and S4 exhibited an increase of 2.42–2.64% of the ground area, compared to more than 7% in S1 and S2, organized around sunlight alone. Sunlight access can therefore be raised substantially, without losing dwellings, at a winter wind cost governed by block configuration rather than building coverage, so densification need not displace the environmental burden from one dimension of liveability to another. As the comparison covers one complex under a single wind direction, it establishes the order of the alternatives and the degree of contrast between them, but not the absolute magnitude of the winter wind cost.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The very high-energy (E &gt; 100 GeV) afterglow emission in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) can be explained by synchrotron self-Compton (SSC). Modeling this emission accurately requires fully numerical codes that solve the time-dependent coupled particle–photon kinetic equations while accounting for Klein–Nishina suppression. However, their substantial computational cost makes them impractical for traditional parameter inference techniques such as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. In this work, we present a highly efficient surrogate model based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) that emulates a one-zone kinetic SSC radiation code. To train our ANN, we use a multi-dimensional model parameter grid that constitutes a sample of 100,800 spectra produced by an infinitely thin spherical blast wave propagating inside a constant density interstellar medium (ISM). The ANN reproduces the numerical spectra well, with the median relative error generally below 2 per cent across the full frequency domain. Using this surrogate framework, we perform Bayesian parameter posterior estimation via MCMC and fit the broadband GRB afterglow observations of GRB 190114C from X-rays to TeV γ-rays at different epochs. We find an energetic jet with isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of Ek, iso ≃ 7.2 × 1054 erg moving with a coasting bulk Lorentz factor of Γ ≳ 500 into an ISM with density n ≃ 0.1 cm−3. The deviation of our model light curve from observations on long timescales suggests that an ISM environment is inconsistent, and instead favours a radially stratified external medium.</jats:p>

title: Multi-objective energy optimization in intelligent grids with high renewable penetration
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As renewable energy sources enter into smart grids, the intermittency, uncertainty, storage coordination, operational cost, carbon emissions and stability of these grids will pose significant challenges. Optimization techniques in conventional systems or rule-based energy management systems are not able to adapt to the fast changes of operating conditions continuously. This paper proposes a Multi-Objective Adaptive Deep Reinforcement Learning (MO-ADRL) framework for real-time optimization of energy in the intelligent grid with high renewable energy penetration. Energy management is formulated as a sequential decision-making problem, and an actor–critic deep reinforcement learning architecture computes continuous dispatch actions. The agent has a Temporal Transformer module which forecasts short-term electricity demand and renewable generation to make proactive decisions. The algorithm contains an adaptive multi-objective reward mechanism which dynamically balances the operational cost, carbon emission, utilization of renewable energy, renewable curtailment, peak demand, battery degradation, and energy supply reliability. Prioritized experience replay is integrated so that transitions with large temporal-difference errors, which usually correspond to critical grid events, are revisited more often during training. The proposed framework achieves real time coordination of solar PV, wind, battery energy storage, grid electricity and flexible demand. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms rule-based energy management, PSO, GA, DQN, DDPG, PPO and SAC for renewable penetration levels from 40% to 80%. At 80% penetration, MO-ADRL lowers the daily operating cost by 31.11% and CO₂ emissions by 38.09% relative to rule-based management, raises renewable utilization to 96.8%, reduces peak demand by 33.76% and keeps supply reliability at 99.6%. MO-ADRL therefore offers an adaptive and scalable route to autonomous energy management in future renewable-dominated intelligent grids.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Differential compaction and diagenesis produce depth-dependent changes in the petrophysical properties of deep tight sandstone and adjacent mudstone. Overlapping P-wave impedance distributions can hinder conventional reservoir prediction, creating an impedance trap. Using well logs from three wells in the Songliao Basin, China, we compare the ability of P-wave impedance and density to distinguish sandstone from mudstone at depths of 3000–4700 m. Two metrics quantify their separation: the probability-density overlap area (Soa) and the separation coefficient (Dsc). P-wave impedance increases in both lithologies, but its discrimination capability improves only slightly with depth. Density shows a contrasting trend: mudstone becomes denser, whereas sandstone density changes little. The density overlap area decreases from approximately 0.8 to 0.3, and its separation coefficient increases from approximately 0.5 to 1.8. The deep intervals exhibit three density endmembers: high-density mudstone, medium-density tight sandstone, and low-density high-quality sandstone. We then apply noise-resistant density inversion (NRDI) to extract a density-gradient AVO attribute from field seismic gathers. In the studied dataset, this attribute delineates deep sand bodies and minor faults more clearly than conventional post-stack attributes. These results support the use of density contrasts to complement impedance-based interpretation in deep tight sandstone reservoirs, subject to adequate amplitude fidelity, angle coverage, and lithological contrast.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Advancing zinc−air batteries (ZABs) critically hinges on developing high-activity and durable catalysts to accelerate the sluggish oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) kinetics. Herein, high-density Fe−N−C active sites was engineered on hollow porous carbon nanofibers via coaxial electrospinning and pyrolysis. The regulatory effect of iron-phenanthroline (Fe−Phen) loading (0.02, 0.06, 0.10 g) on the material structural properties and catalytic ORR performance was systematically investigated. Multidimensional characterizations and electrochemical test results reveal that insufficient precursor loading results in scarce active sites, while overloading induces agglomeration of metal species and structural collapse of the fibrous framework during pyrolysis, both of which greatly compromise catalytic efficiency. At the optimal Fe−Phen loading of 0.06 g, the resultant Fe-HPCNFs catalyst simultaneously achieves high-density distribution of Fe−N−C sites, and a well-developed intact hierarchical pore microstructure. Benefiting from the synergistically optimization, the Fe-HPCNFs exhibits excellent ORR properties with a half-wave potential of 0.84 V in 0.1 M KOH. When applied as the cathode catalyst in a liquid ZABs, it delivers a high specific capacity of 805 mAh g−1 and outstanding long-term cycling stability over 450 h. This study offers a promising synthetic route for high-performance ORR electrocatalysts, providing meaningful guidance for the design of advanced cathode materials toward ZABs applications.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>The development of highly efficient and durable dual-functional electrocatalysts for overall water splitting is significant for renewable hydrogen production. abstract: <jats:p>Dielectric capacitors are essential components in pulsed-power and power-electronic systems, but their limited energy density remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, polymorphic polar nanoregions (PNRs) are constructed in lead-free high-entropy (1−x)[0.85(Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-0.15BaTiO3]-xSr(Ta0.6Mg0.3Hf0.1)O3 relaxor ferroelectric ceramics by introducing heterovalent Sr2+, Mg2+, Ta5+, and Hf4+ ions under charge conservation. The increased configurational entropy and local chemical disorder disrupt long-range ferroelectric order, splitting domains into atomic-scale PNRs (&lt;10 nm) and creating a polymorphic R–O–T/C polar network with multiple polarization switching channels. The optimal x = 0.2 ceramic achieves a recoverable energy density of 11.07 J cm−3 with 91.5% efficiency at 588 kV cm−1. It also maintains stable energy storage from 20 to 110 °C and over 106 cycles, and delivers a fast discharge time t0.9 of 104 ns with a power density of 94.8 MW cm−3. This polymorphic PNR strategy provides a promising route for high-performance lead-free capacitive energy storage.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>White light-excited afterglow carbon dots (CDs) with controllable time-dependent emission are highly desirable for advanced optical security but remain challenging because precisely regulating the evolution of multiple long-lived emissive states is difficult. Herein, we report a matrix-confinement and interfacial-engineering strategy to construct white light-excited afterglow CD composites by integrating CDs into borate and borate–silica hybrid matrices. The resulting G-CDs@B2O3 and G-CDs@SiO2@B2O3 exhibit distinct yellow-to-green and green-to-yellow afterglow evolution under white light excitation. Structural characterization reveals that the rigid borate matrix stabilizes the emissive states through abundant B–O, B–OH, and B–C interactions, whereas the introduction of an APTES-derived silicate network creates additional Si–O–C and Si–C interfacial interactions that redistribute the relative contributions of multiple emissive states without altering the core structure of CDs. Benefiting from these unique dynamic optical properties, the composites enable time-resolved anticounterfeiting and information encryption with enhanced security.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We analyze the photometric and spectroscopic data for AT 2023rcq, a transient flare hosted in the quasar SDSS J014926.13+074311.1 at redshift
                    <jats:italic>z</jats:italic>
                    = 0.539. The flare appeared to have optical light curves of a tidal disruption event (TDE) type, i.e., a fast rise followed with a slow decay, and was accompanied with a delayed mid-infrared (MIR) flare. More interestingly, a high-energy (HE) neutrino event IC-240327A was found to be detected at the time of the MIR flare. Such temporal and positional coincidence cases have been found for TDEs and the nuclear accretion flares with strong accompanying MIR flares, suggesting TDEs and the accretion flares as potential HE-neutrino emitters. We determine the properties of AT 2023rcq. Based on the results from the light-curve fitting and spectral analysis, in which an optical spectrum obtained by us during the flare is used, AT 2023rcq is likely not a TDE. Also the strength of its MIR flare is relatively weak compared to the sample of the nuclear accretion flares. We discuss AT 2023rcq as a case that may represent a sample of similar properties. Investigations to build such a sample and their possible association with HE neutrinos are warranted.
                  </jats:p>
