abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how CEO–board social-tie density and compatibility influence investment efficiency and M&A announcement performance, with board co-option and disclosure readability as moderating factors. It asks whether relational proximity improves decision quality or weakens governance, and whether these effects are nonlinear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a panel of 612 nonfinancial firms from the S&P 1,500 and STOXX Europe 600 during 2010–2024, the study constructs CEO–board ties from shared employment, education and associations. Investment efficiency is estimated from standard investment models, and M&A performance is measured by short-window acquirer cumulative abnormal returns . Hierarchical regressions with fixed effects are complemented by robustness and 2SLS tests.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CEO–board social-tie density exhibits a concave association with both investment efficiency and M&A announcement returns, consistent with the predicted inverted U-shaped pattern. Moderate tie density improves coordination and information exchange, whereas excessive density weakens independent challenge. Compatibility strengthens the beneficial association between tie density and investment efficiency and shifts its turning point toward higher levels, whereas co-option shifts the turning point toward lower levels. In M&A settings, greater disclosure readability strengthens the favorable association between tie density and announcement returns.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes by showing how CEO–board relational structures shape firm-level investment and acquisition outcomes through a nonlinear agency-advisory mechanism. Rather than treating CEO–board ties as uniformly harmful or beneficial, it demonstrates that their consequences depend on where firms lie on the relational-density spectrum and on how compatibility and co-option condition that position. It advances a contingent view of relational governance by linking boardroom social structure to both internal capital-allocation efficiency and market-based acquisition outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract: <jats:p>High-viscosity metallocene poly(α-olefins) are important synthetic lubricant base oils. However, the effects of molecular structure on permanent viscosity loss during mechanical shearing remain insufficiently understood. In this study, mPAO with varying monomer carbon numbers, kinematic viscosities, molecular weight distributions, chain stereoregularities, and residual unsaturation levels were investigated using KRL shear testing, gel permeation chromatography, and spectroscopic characterization. The results showed that the number-average molecular weight decreased and the molecular weight distribution broadened after shearing, whereas the weight-average molecular weight changed only slightly, suggesting that molecular weight changes primarily involved a fraction of the polymer chains. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed oxidation-related changes after shearing, suggesting that oxidation-induced viscosity increase may partially offset shear-induced viscosity loss. Different side-chain structures exhibited distinct shear responses as the monomer carbon number varied. For samples with similar side-chain structures, the viscosity loss rate increased nonlinearly and in a stepwise manner with increasing backbone length. A broader initial molecular weight distribution was associated with greater PVL, whereas higher chain stereoregularity and lower residual unsaturation were associated with improved shear stability. These findings clarify the relationships between molecular structural parameters and the mechanical shear stability of mPAO, providing a basis for designing high-viscosity lubricant base oils with improved shear stability.</jats:p>

title: Aplicabilidade da captura de movimentos inerciais para avaliar riscos biomecânicos Applicability of inertial motion capture for assessing biomechanical risks
abstract: <jats:p>Na ergonomia, a avaliação precisa de posturas e cargas de trabalho é essencial para diminuir os riscos biomecânicos e reduzir a incidência de lesões musculoesqueléticas. Isso é importante, particularmente para usuários vulneráveis durante a realização de atividade física, como pessoas com ausência de membro superior. Nesse contexto, a utilização de sensores inerciais possibilita a coleta de dados quantitativos, o que complementa a observação direta e favorece a tomada de decisão. Assim, o atual estudo tem como objetivo avaliar os riscos biomecânicos em atividades simuladas, levando em consideração as capacidades e limitações de um usuário com prótese de membro superior, por meio da captura de movimentos inerciais. Quanto à metodologia, o estudo caracteriza-se como aplicado - com abordagem mista e objetivo exploratório. Em relação aos procedimentos técnicos, foi realizado um estudo de caso, tendo a divisão em duas fases, sendo: (i) Pré-coleta e (ii) Avaliação ergonômica por meio do software ScaleFit Industrial Athlete. Para fase (ii) foram avaliadas as atividades de: vestir um casaco, carregar um cesto de roupas e carregar uma mochila. Como resultado, foi possível verificar posturas e ângulos desfavoráveis assumidas pela usuária da coleta, envolvendo variáveis como frequência e valor máximo, unindo a identificação de possíveis riscos com a observação direta de filmagens e comparação com estudos correlatos.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Reliable multi-horizon forecasting of electricity demand is vital for effective scheduling, planning, and operational decision-making in contemporary power systems. This paper introduces a computationally efficient framework for real-time forecasting using a Stacked Reservoir Computing Architecture (SRCA) with dynamic horizon fusion and ridge-regularized readout. The proposed framework captures nonlinear temporal interactions using hierarchically stacked reservoirs with fixed internal dynamics in order to reduce gradient-based training alongside significant pre-processing. To ensure consistency and temporal continuity across the forecast horizons, the model employs a dynamic horizon-fusion mechanism that adaptively blends the horizon-specific outputs generated by the ridge-regularized readout layer. Furthermore, the system includes raw-mode Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) features that enhance signal diversity and representational depth without complicating the model. A comprehensive ablation study and statistical validation process further identified the optimal configuration awhich shows strong predictive performance, with MAPE values of 1.17% and 2.82% and R2 scores of 0.989 and 0.973, respectively, across two real-world electricity demand datasets. Comparative evaluation further shows that forecast-aware variational mode decomposition (FA-CVMD) reduces the average root mean square error (RMSE) by 2.13% and 37.33% compared with forecast-aware complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition (FA-CEMD) on the two datasets, respectively. The SRCA framework requires shorter training time, making it suitable for quick and adaptable forecasting. The results demonstrate that the suggested architecture is a suitable and computationally efficient multi-horizon load forecasting method for current power systems.</jats:p>

title: Effective density of states of a dissipative and confined cyclotron motion

abstract: <jats:p>We determine the effective thermodynamic density of states associated with the reduced partition function of a charged two-dimensional harmonic oscillator in a uniform magnetic field and linearly coupled to an Ohmic heat bath regularized by a Drude cutoff. The reduced partition function is factorized exactly in terms of the complex decay rates of the two magnetic chiral sectors and gamma functions. A weak-coupling expansion nonperturbatively in a magnetic field resolves the bath-induced ground-state shift into the two chiral Fock–Darwin modes. Its inverse Laplace transform contains an isolated contribution at the reduced ground-state energy defined by the partition-function ratio and a continuum that starts immediately above it. The low-energy continuum is fixed by the Ohmic bath, while the high-energy density grows linearly as required by the two-dimensional classical limit. We derive the residue representation for generic nondegenerate magnetic-field poles and show why the zero-field limit requires separate treatment when chiral pole pairs coalesce. High-precision inverse-Laplace calculations are combined with the analytic residue expansion to obtain numerically stable continuum densities from threshold to high energy. Dissipation progressively suppresses the oscillatory spectral structure, whereas the magnetic field reorganizes the resonance positions and weights and invalidates a literal extension of the usual zero-field all-real-pole overdamped classification. The zero-field calculation is independently validated against the damped-oscillator density of states of Hanke and Zwerger. We also emphasize that the resulting quantity is an effective thermodynamic density of states defined by the reduced partition function rather than the local spectral function of the open subsystem.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sodium titanium phosphate (NaTi2(PO4)3, NTP), a promising sodium superionic conductor (NASICON)-type anode for aqueous sodium-ion batteries, suffers from severe capacity fade in alkaline electrolytes due to dissolution of Ti via soluble titanate formation. Herein, we introduce an iron-doping-enabled dual-scale confinement strategy that delivers high capacity and exceptional stability. Iron incorporation in NTP induces a solubility limited behavior: a fraction of Fe enters the NASICON lattice, while excess Fe migrates toward the surface to form a partially amorphous Fe3O4 shell, creating cooperative bulk-shell architecture. The iron-rich outer layer, populated with redox-active Fe3+/Fe2+ couples, acts as a barrier that intercepts and consumes inward-diffusing OH– ions, while inner Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reactions competitively consume residual OH– within the lattice, thereby effectively suppressing soluble titanate formation. This study confirms a synergistic self-protecting and capacity-enhancing mechanism for NTP-based anode design. Consequently, the as-prepared anode delivers a high specific capacity of 164.9 mAh g–1 among all reported NTP anodes, while retaining 90.9% of its initial capacity after 2000 cycles, significantly outperforming previous benchmarks. Paired with a Ni–Co layered double hydroxide cathode, the full cell delivers a high energy density of 106.4 Wh kg–1. This self-organized core–shell dual-defense architecture provides a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing electrodes in corrosive environments.</jats:p>

title: Prediksi Aktivitas Antioksidan Senyawa Bioaktif Menggunakan Pendekatan Machine Learning Berbasis Deskriptor Molekul
journal: KUADRAN: Jurnal Analitika Data dan Ilmu Komputer
abstract:
<jats:p>Purpose: This study builds machine learning models that predict the DPPH radical-scavenging activity of phenolic acids from simple, mechanistically designed molecular descriptors, and examines which structural features drive the activity.
Design/Methodology: Activity data (pTEAC) for 21 phenolic acids measured under a single protocol were taken from Jing et al. (2012), keeping the original split of 15 training and 6 test compounds. Fifteen two-dimensional descriptors were computed, including the number and position of hydroxyl and methoxy groups, electron-donating groups ortho/para to the phenolic OH, conjugation, TPSA, and Hammett constants. Multiple linear regression, partial least squares, k-nearest neighbours, support vector regression, and random forest were compared using leave-one-out cross-validation, an external test set, 100-fold Y-randomization, permutation importance, and a leverage-based applicability domain.
Findings: Random forest performed best (Q²LOO = 0.892; external R²pred = 0.767) and passed Y-randomization, while k-NN and SVR overfitted. The number of electron-donating groups ortho/para to the phenolic OH and TPSA dominated the model. A two-descriptor linear equation was interpretable but statistically weak (Q²LOO = 0.409). The 2D models remained below published 3D CoMFA/CoMSIA models (R²pred ≈ 0.98); most of the test error came from one compound flagged as outside the applicability domain.
Practical Implications: The workflow can be used to rank phenolic compounds from natural extracts before laboratory testing, provided that predictions are restricted to the applicability domain.
Originality/Value: The study combines transparent mechanism-based descriptors with a complete OECD-oriented validation on real experimental data and reports honestly where the 2D approach falls short of 3D models.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With the development of inertial confinement fusion facilities, the surface cleanliness of key optical components has become increasingly important for stable system operation. Conventional cleaning methods can remove organic contaminants to some extent, but residual control, secondary contamination, and process compatibility may still be challenging in ultra‐clean optical applications. Low‐pressure plasma cleaning offers low‐residue processing and reduced risk of secondary contamination. However, the cleaning mechanism and process regularities of plasma cleaning for fused silica optical components remain insufficiently understood, and systematic optimization of process parameters is still limited. Using dibutyl phthalate (DBP) as a representative organic contaminant, this study systematically investigates the adsorption behavior of DBP on fused silica, its decomposition mechanism under low‐pressure oxygen plasma, and the effects of cleaning time and power on cleaning effectiveness, thereby providing a basis for optimizing low‐pressure plasma cleaning processes. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the physical adsorption of organic contaminants on fused silica, and white‐light interferometry was employed to characterize the surface morphology of fused silica components under different contamination states. Single‐factor and full‐factorial experiments were further conducted to evaluate the effects of cleaning time and power on contaminant removal, followed by optimization of these process parameters using response surface methodology. The results clarify the reaction pathway for DBP decomposition during low‐pressure plasma cleaning and identify reasonable cleaning parameters through process optimization, providing theoretical support and experimental data for low‐pressure plasma cleaning of ultra‐clean optical components.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Constitutive surrogates for nanosilica- and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-modified engineered cementitious composites (ECCs) may reduce the cost of evaluating compressive stress–strain responses across mix designs. This study benchmarks data-driven, spline-based, operator-learning, and physics-regularized architectures using 24 digitized experimental curves, one per mixture, resampled to 737 within-curve collocation points; the composition-level sample size is therefore 24, and no specimen-level replicates were available. Random pointwise and blind-mixture validation are compared to distinguish within-curve interpolation from prediction for unseen mixtures. Across repeated five-mixture hold-outs, XGBoost achieved the lowest mean RMSE: 2.56±0.21 MPa over six splits and 2.77±0.61 MPa over fifteen splits compared with 3.41±0.88 MPa for the automatically selected (zero-physics-weight) neural network over the same fifteen splits (exact two-sided Wilcoxon W=9, unadjusted p=0.002; the splits overlap and are not independent replicates). On the principal blind split, this automatically selected neural-network configuration achieved R2=0.9930 and RMSE =1.81 MPa; however, its selected physics-loss weights were zero, so this is a data-only result and does not establish an improvement due to physical regularization. Adding damage and smoothness penalties to the perceptron increased its blind RMSE (to 4.96 MPa or 5.72 MPa, depending on the weights). Under non-matched physics objectives, a 576-parameter spline network with an elastic-modulus penalty achieved R2=0.9810 and RMSE =2.98 MPa compared with R2=0.9302 and RMSE =5.72 MPa for a 6368-weight perceptron trained with all three penalties; this contrast cannot be attributed to architecture alone. The soft damage-boundedness and smoothness penalties did not guarantee monotonic damage evolution or complete constitutive admissibility; the damage measure used is an apparent stiffness-degradation indicator rather than a validated damage law for fiber-bridged ECC, and Gaussian-process intervals covered 86.2% (89.9% after recalibration) of blind points against a nominal 95%. Differences between digitized and companion-study tabulated peak properties (up to 27.3% in peak stress) remain unresolved, so all performance statements are conditional on the digitized benchmark. These findings support mixture-level validation, the careful attribution of physics-regularization effects, and the verification of source data before any deployment in nonlinear structural simulations.</jats:p>

title: MACHINE-LEARNING CROP CLASSIFICATION UNDER IDEALIZED TEMPERATURE AND RAINFALL PERTURBATIONS Proyección mediante aprendizaje automático de los cambios en la idoneidad de los cultivos bajo los escenarios climáticos del IPCC: una recomendación
abstract:
<jats:p>Machine-learning crop recommenders are increasingly proposed for climate adaptation, yet the benchmark data behind them are rarely examined. We audited the public Crop Recommendation Dataset (2,200 records, 22 crops, seven soil and climate inputs), compared eight classifiers in a leakage-controlled pipeline and submitted the fitted models to idealized perturbations of temperature (+1.5 to +4 °C) and rainfall (±10 and ±20%). Each crop occupies fixed-width, uniformly filled ranges, a structure consistent with records generated from predefined intervals. Random Forest reached 99.36% five-fold accuracy, statistically indistinguishable from Extra Trees, while label permutations stayed at chance; thirteen engineered features did not raise accuracy. Rainfall changes reassigned up to 8.0% of records, against at most 0.6% for warming alone; the hottest and driest case reassigned 10.1% and placed 17.2% of records outside the applicability domain. Other classifiers responded more strongly but ranked the perturbations alike. A generic alert flag rose from 15.7% to 18.3%, a value governed by crop composition and threshold choice. The predicted class reproduces benchmark labels, not validated agronomic suitability; the protocol offers a transparent stress test for crop classifiers before they inform climate adaptation.
Keywords: random forest; sensitivity analysis; applicability domain; agro-environmental alerts; data provenance.</jats:p>

title: Measuring the Hermeneutic Circle in Explainable AI: A Human-Free Test Based on Data Horizons, Executable Claims, Part–Whole Agreement, and Machine Readers

affiliation.name: Department of Computer Science, Erik Jonsson School of Engineering and Computer Science, The University of Texas at Dallas, Richardson, TX 75080, USA
Department of Software Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Haliç University, 34060 Istanbul, Türkiye

abstract: <jats:p>Explanations of machine learning models are read by people but rarely evaluated with them, and automatic metrics score attribution vectors rather than what a reader receives. We operationalise the horizon, the hermeneutic circle, and the hermeneutics of suspicion as the Hermeneutic Circle Test (HCT), a human-free screen for explanations of tabular classifiers. HCT checks whether an explanation’s evidence lies inside a calibrated data horizon, whether its sentences survive on-horizon interventions, whether its account of a case agrees with the whole model and at which scale, and whether it helps machine readers learn the model. Over seven explainers, four datasets, and two model families (mean ± standard deviation over eight settings), the best explainer, KernelSHAP, verified 0.65 ± 0.15 of its claims, while random attributions verified 0.22 ± 0.08. On the same explanations, established faithfulness, remove-and-retrain, and disagreement metrics missed impossible evidence and narratives contradicting their own attributions, and sign-blind metrics scored sign-flipped explanations like the originals. Claim tests withstood scaffold attacks that adapt to the horizon and to the test itself; a scaffold that memorises the audited records weakened them and deceived every explainer, but part–whole agreement still flagged it. HCT is a reproducible screen to apply before user studies.</jats:p>

title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils

abstract: <jats:p>Determining the biological sex of the individuals who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils remains challenging due to the absence of ground truth, morphological differences between contemporary and prehistoric populations, and uncertainties arising from image degradation. Traditional morphometric methods are further constrained by substantial overlap between sexes, limited cross-population generalizability, and subjective feature selection. This study introduces a deep learning framework that explicitly models, propagates, and aggregates uncertainty throughout the analytical pipeline. As a proof of concept, each stencil is represented by twelve plausible silhouette realizations to account for boundary uncertainty, which are processed by two ensembles of ten deep neural networks trained on contemporary hand samples to learn potentially transferable morphological patterns. A triangulated validation scheme integrates ensemble predictions, two-dimensional latent-space analysis, and spatial attribution maps to assess the consistency of the results from complementary perspectives. Applied to prehistoric hand stencils, the framework produces sex predictions alongside confidence measures based on internal agreement, helping distinguish morphologically consistent cases from ambiguous ones. The combined evidence from ensemble predictions, latent-space organization, and spatial attribution demonstrates the potential of explicitly quantifying uncertainty in archaeological inference, providing a systematic and interpretable approach to the analysis of prehistoric hand art.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>This review examined machine learning applications to adolescent sports injury prediction. Six databases were searched on 25 May 2026 for publications from January 2021 onward involving participants aged 10–19 years. Two reviewers independently screened studies. Methodological appraisal was conducted using PROBAST+AI, design-specific JBI checklists, or QualSyst, with one reviewer conducting the assessments and the other verifying them. Findings were synthesized narratively. Thirty reports representing 29 studies covered injury prediction, clinical and surrogate outcomes, biomechanical classification, and monitoring or exploratory applications. Thirteen reports provided ROC-AUC values of 0.58–0.94; sensitivity/recall for injury occurrence or recurrence ranged from 25.0% to 94.3%. Features included maturation, anthropometry, clinical history, neuromuscular performance, biomechanics, physiological and metabolic markers, training load, and psychological and sleep-related measures. Among 14 PROBAST+AI reports, performance-related risk of bias was high in 4 and unclear in 10. JBI assessments identified methodological concerns; nine QualSyst scores ranged from 0.50 to 0.80, with one report unscored owing to indeterminate criterion applicability. Evidence is insufficient to establish the generalizability of machine-learning performance because of high or unclear risk of bias and limited external validation. Addressing these limitations may support the future use of machine learning in sports injury risk prediction among adolescents. The review was prospectively registered with OSF (PYE97) and received no external funding.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>Crop yield prediction based on environmental, soil, water, and weather parameters has become a
vital area of research, addressing the growing need for sustainable agricultural practices and
food security. This study adopts a machine learning approach to optimize crop yield production
within the agricultural landscape of Michika Local Government Area, Adamawa State. Applying
extensive crop datasets, machine learning techniques are utilized to analyze, interpret, and
uncover critical factors and patterns influencing crop yields. The main objective is to develop a
robust predictive model that empowers farmers and stakeholders with actionable insights, to
enhance agricultural productivity. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in yield
predicting accuracy through machine learning-based methods compared to traditional
approaches. ANN with the lowest RMSE (3136.8), the lowest MAE (2502.2), and higher R²
(0.073255), indicates the most accurate predictions. These findings underscore the transformative
potential of artificial intelligence in advancing precision agriculture, enabling resource-efficient
farming, and bolstering food security. This study also highlights avenues for future research,
including optimizing resource allocation strategies, identifying resilient crop varieties, predicting
and mitigating crop diseases, and mapping soil suitability for diverse crops. Such efforts would
further drive the adoption of smart agricultural systems, enhancing productivity and sustainability
while supporting the transition to climate-resilient farming practices.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Environmental sustainability is a result of complex configurations of emissions, air pollution, and environmental infrastructure. This paper investigates environmental sustainability of 154 countries based on four environmental variables and the Natural Capital Protection (NCP) score. Principal component analysis (PCA), K-means clustering, prediction models, and explainable AI techniques, such as SHAP and LIME, in addition to network and persistent-homology analysis, are utilized as part of the methodology. Two principal components accounted for 74.70% of the total variance. Five environmental groups were identified to facilitate an interpretation of cross-country heterogeneity. PM2.5 turned out to be the most important model-assigned predictor of NCP, followed by methane and carbon emissions, while water access was the one with the lowest SHAP value on average. Network and persistent-homology analysis provided additional information about patterns of model attributions as well as about the relationships between environmental indicators.</jats:p>

title: Predicting the Mechanical Properties of Concrete Containing Basalt Fiber Utilizing Optimized Hybrid Machine Learning Modeling

abstract: <jats:p>Basalt-fiber-reinforced concrete (BFRC) has attracted increasing attention owing to its potential to enhance concrete performance under different loading conditions. Because of the complex interactions among mixture constituents and fiber characteristics, predicting its mechanical properties can be challenging. Therefore, this study develops six individual machine learning (ML) models and a hybrid ML model based on weighted voting techniques using the six developed learners to predict both the compressive strength (CS) and tensile strength (TS) of BFRC. The individual ML models include K-nearest neighbors (KNN), random forest (RF), extra trees regressor (ETR), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), Light GBM (LightGBM), and gradient boosting machine (GBM). The hyperparameter optimization is performed using both particle swarm optimization (PSO) and grey wolf optimizer (GWO). Additionally, a superior hybrid ML model based on the six learners is constructed to improve the prediction accuracy of CS and TS of BFRC. Two datasets with the same mixtures containing 227 samples each were compiled from literature using eight input features: cement (C), coarse aggregate-to-fine aggregate ratio (CAG/FAG), silica fume/cement (SF/C), fly ash/cement (FA/C), water/cement ratio (W/C), superplasticizer/cement (SP/C), basalt fiber length-to-diameter ratio (F_LD), and fiber content (F_%). Analysis reveals that SF/C has the greatest influence on CS predictions, followed by W/C, CAG/FAG, F_%, and C, while TS predictions are mostly influenced by CAG/FAG, W/C, F_LD, and F_%. Finally, a graphical user interface (GUI) is developed for predicting BFRC strengths using the base learners and the hybrid model.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>A novel computational framework that integrates the mechanistic rigor of Pharmacometrics (PMx) with the predictive power of Multimodal Machine Learning (MML) is conceptually formulated and discussed. The framework is designed to address critical developmental bottlenecks in the drug development sector, which is already witnessing a paradigm shift driven by the rise of Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs)—a class that, according to recent pipeline analyses, accounts for an expanding share of innovative oncology trials. Unfortunately, despite the therapeutic promise of ADCs and other targeted modalities, the industry faces a productivity paradox, characterized by high attrition rates in transitional clinical phases and a median development timeline of seven years. By leveraging transfer learning strategies, we delineate how the synergistic adoption of PMx and MML can conceptually optimize dose selection, inform metastatic risk assessment through genomic-imaging integration, and ultimately accelerate the transition from bench to bedside. This is conceptualized through the definition of methodologies capable of transforming noisy early-phase clinical data into actionable insights, thus bridging the gap between Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling and deep learning-driven outcomes. Without advancing premature empirical claims, we establish a structured methodological roadmap for a scalable, AI-enhanced clinical trial infrastructure, positioning hybrid modeling as a viable architectural paradigm for the next generation of precision oncology.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Electric motors are the principal power units of industry, and their failures cause cascading stoppages of process equipment. The vibration signal carries the most complete information about the condition of rotating assemblies, yet machine-learning diagnostics is constrained by the shortage of labelled fault data. This work proposes and verifies a methodology for generating a physically grounded synthetic dataset of vibration signals: analytical models of imbalance, misalignment, rolling-bearing defects (BPFO, BPFI, BSF, FTF) and mechanical looseness produced 8000 one-second fragments of vibration acceleration covering eight classes of technical state, with variation of the rotational frequency (±5%), signal-to-noise ratio (5–30 dB) and defect amplitude. The synthetic signals were verified against reference Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) records: the outer- and inner-ring defect frequencies agree within 0.22%, and the envelope spectra are class-specific for these defects. Six classifiers were compared in three stages: Random Forest, XGBoost, a 1D-CNN (WDCNN), two 2D-CNNs on STFT and CWT representations, and a PatchTST transformer. Under the full set of variations, models reached a Macro F1 of 99.6–99.8%. On the real CWRU records, separate models were trained on the dataset based on real data from other operating loads. On the unseen loads, the Random Forest reached a Macro F1 of 95.5% and the 1D-CNN 93.2%, against 21–42% for the same models trained on synthetic data alone, and with one real fragment per class, the difference between the two training datasets was already 17–32 p.p. High accuracy on synthetic data therefore did not carry over to zero-shot diagnosis on the real bench.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plurigaussian simulation (PGS) is a powerful approach in generating discrete stochastic structures of complex multiphase systems across a range of scales. Originating as an extension of truncated Gaussian simulation, PGS allows for the detailed representation of phase relationships and connectivity. A key element of PGS is the identification of truncation rules to dictate the geometric and facies relationships and traditionally involves a trial-and-error approach based on the physical characteristics of the modelled structures. The purpose of this study is to present an approach to learning such rules.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study introduces the use of generative adversarial networks, specifically using the Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty architecture, to automate and enhance the selection of truncation rules through a neural truncation rule.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By learning directly from the characteristics of the training data, this approach aims to bypass the limitations of manual truncation rule selection, offering a more efficient and precise method to replicate the desired structural features.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study highlights the efficacy of generative machine learning in identifying suitable truncation rules for PGS, significantly reducing the uncertainty in truncation rule choice and enabling the accurate realisation of complex structural characteristics without the ill-informed trial-and-error process traditionally undertaken.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Context—Recruitment has become a multidimensional decision-making process in which organizations must evaluate both qualitative and quantitative candidate attributes simultaneously. While machine iearning (ML) methods are effective for predicting recruitment outcomes and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques provide structured ranking mechanisms, these approaches are commonly applied independently. As a result, the advantages of predictive analytics and expert-based evaluation are not fully utilized within a unified decision-support processObjective—This study proposes a hybrid decision-support framework that integrates ML and MCDM techniques to improve personnel selection. The framework is designed to combine data-driven prediction with systematic multi-criteria evaluation, while also examining the relative importance of recruitment criteria and the consistency of alternative ranking methods.Method—The proposed methodology consists of two sequential stages. First, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting Tree algorithms are developed using a publicly available recruitment dataset, and their predictive performances are comparatively evaluated to identify the most suitable model. The predicted hiring probabilities are then used to shortlist the most promising candidates. In the second stage, these candidates are evaluated using an integrated MCDM framework. Criterion weights are determined through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), whereas candidate rankings are generated using TOPSIS, ELECTRE, and VIKOR. Finally, Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient is employed to examine the degree of agreement among the rankings obtained from the different MCDM methods.Results—Among the evaluated ML algorithms, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Tree demonstrated closely comparable predictive performance. Gradient Boosting Tree was retained for candidate screening because it achieved slightly higher recall, F1-score, and test ROC–AUC. The integration of predicted hiring probabilities into the MCDM stage enabled a more focused evaluation of shortlisted candidates. TOPSIS, ELECTRE, and VIKOR consistently identified the same highest-ranked candidate, although varying degrees of agreement were observed across the remaining candidate rankings. Furthermore, the AHP results identified Interview (0.5031) and Personality (0.2316) as the most influential criteria, followed by Education (0.1481), Skill (0.0755), and Experience (0.0417).Conclusion—The proposed hybrid framework effectively combines predictive modeling with multi-criteria evaluation in a unified decision-support environment. By linking ML predictions with transparent ranking techniques, the framework improves the reliability and interpretability of recruitment decisions. Owing to its flexible structure, the proposed approach can be adapted to various industrial engineering applications and other decision-making problems involving multiple evaluation criteria.</jats:p>

title: Using AI and Machine Learning to Advance Nucleic Acid Therapeutic Delivery Beyond the Liver

affiliation.name: University of Connecticut
University of Connecticut

abstract:
<jats:p>Researchers can now design nucleic acid medicines for specific genetic targets, but
delivering those medicines to the right cells and tissues remains a major challenge. Advances in
nucleic acid therapeutics have greatly expanded treatment options for various genetic and metabolic
diseases, especially those affecting the liver. Beyond chemical stabilization of nucleic acids, much of
the progress has come from achieving efficient, cell-specific delivery. A key factor in this success is
the development of chemically engineered bioconjugates, such as the N-acetylgalactosamine ligand,
which binds selectively to hepatocyte receptors in the liver. This allows for highly efficient delivery of
small interfering RNA and antisense oligonucleotides. However, replicating this delivery efficiency
in tissues outside the liver (extrahepatic) remains a major challenge. The main obstacle is the lack of
well-defined ligand–receptor pairs that mediate cell-specific recognition and uptake in extrahepatic
organs. This discussion paper examines how artificial intelligence and machine learning can accelerate
the discovery of new chemical ligands for targeted nucleic acid delivery to tissues outside the liver.
Taken together, the methods these tools support could enable targeting of organs that are difficult
to reach with nucleic acid-based therapies and broaden treatment options for certain cancers and
metabolic disorders for which additional treatments are needed.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Cybersecurity: Impact on Threat Detection and Incident Response

affiliation.name: Department of Business and Technology, Webster University, St. Louis, MO 63119, USA

journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>The increasing sophistication, volume, and velocity of cyber threats have rendered traditional rulebased and signature-driven cybersecurity mechanisms increasingly inadequate. Modern attacks,
such as zero-day exploits, ransomware, advanced persistent threats, and insider attacks, operate
with high adaptability and stealth, overwhelming conventional security systems and delaying
effective incident response. In response, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)
have emerged as critical enablers of intelligent, adaptive, and automated cybersecurity defenses.
This study systematically reviews existing literature to examine the impact of AI and ML on
cybersecurity, with a specific focus on threat detection and incident response. Adopting a
Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology, the study synthesizes peer-reviewed academic
articles and high-quality industry reports published between 2018 and 2024, sourced from major
databases including Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. The review analyzes
how supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning, and deep learning techniques are applied
across cybersecurity domains such as intrusion detection, malware classification, behavioural
analytics, and automated incident response. The findings reveal that AI-driven cybersecurity
systems significantly enhance detection accuracy, reduce false positives, and substantially
decrease mean time to detection and response. Deep learning models demonstrate superior
performance in identifying complex and previously unseen attack patterns, while reinforcement
learning supports adaptive policy optimization for dynamic threat environments. However, the
review also identifies persistent challenges related to data quality, model interpretability,
adversarial attacks, ethical considerations, and governance constraints. This study, therefore,
advances the conceptual understanding of AI as both an adaptive learning mechanism and a
systemic component within security architectures; and contributes to cybersecurity scholarship by
consolidating fragmented evidence, and offering strategic implications for organizations seeking
resilient, ethical, and scalable AI-driven cybersecurity solutions.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Literature-derived machine learning may guide preclinical cancer nanomedicine, but its value for predicting treatment efficacy depends on what it learns and where its predictions remain reliable. We examined quantitative predictive fidelity, the relative contributions of treatment context and nanoparticle design, and generalization across experimental domains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We independently reanalysed the NanoAnalysis resource of 745 preclinical studies of inorganic nanoparticles in cancer. The released modelling matrix included 397 studies and 130 predictors. Repeated cross-validation assessed classification of &gt;90% tumor-volume reduction relative to untreated controls and prediction of continuous reduction. Feature-family comparisons and grouped permutation analyses examined signal attribution. Last-author-grouped validation, within-corpus chronological tests and domain holdouts benchmarked against random holdouts matched for sample size and outcome-class counts assessed generalization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The full random forest achieved an out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.712 (95% bootstrap confidence interval 0.659–0.763), average precision of 0.688 and Brier score of 0.214. Continuous prediction explained little variation (R
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      = 0.118), with mean absolute error of 12.1 percentage points versus 12.9 for a training-fold median baseline. A 13-feature model comprising therapy modality and combination-therapy status achieved AUC 0.695, whereas nanoparticle-design-only features achieved 0.568. Removing treatment context reduced AUC to 0.607; removing nanoparticle-design features retained 0.686. Last-author grouping had little effect on discrimination, while the latest chronological test included only 30 studies and had wide uncertainty. Iron-oxide holdout AUC was 0.583 versus a matched-random median of 0.709, whereas gold showed little penalty.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Moderate discrimination of high-response studies coexisted with limited prediction of response magnitude. Under the evaluated representation and models, treatment context carried most of the recoverable discriminatory signal, and transferability varied by material domain. For preclinical pharmacology, these findings support context-aware hypothesis generation and emphasize quantitative error and applicability-domain evaluation before using literature-derived predictions to select formulations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>This thesis presents an Enhanced Hybrid Fuzzing Framework designed for testing and identifying
vulnerabilities in concurrent software systems by integrating fuzzy testing, machine learning,
model checking, and concurrency testing techniques. Traditional fuzzing methods often fall short
in detecting subtle bugs, particularly those arising in concurrent environments such as race
conditions and deadlocks. This hybrid framework addresses these limitations by incorporating a
Machine Learning Module that predicts the likelihood of software crashes based on patterns
from previous tests, and a Model Checking system that verifies software correctness across
different states and multi-threaded executions. The framework’s fuzzing engine generates
random or semi-random inputs to test various software behaviors, while the machine learning
component prioritizes high-likelihood crash inputs for more focused testing. The Model Checking
Module evaluates state transitions and thread interactions, allowing the detection of complex
concurrency-related issues. In addition, Error Detection and Reporting mechanisms capture
detailed logs of crashes, stack traces, and anomalies, facilitating deeper analysis and efficient
debugging. The framework was implemented using Python and C++ programming languages,
selected for their flexibility in handling machine learning algorithms, concurrency testing, and
low-level memory operations required for fuzzing. Python was employed for the machine
learning and data handling components, while C++ was used for the fuzzing engine and model
checking due to its performance and system-level capabilities. The results demonstrate the
framework's capability to increase the detection of vulnerabilities in complex software systems,
reduce false positives, and improve efficiency in concurrent software testing. By leveraging the
power of machine learning and model checking, this hybrid approach enhances the software
testing process, contributing to more reliable and secure software development. This abstract
summarizes the key objectives, techniques, and results of the Enhanced Hybrid Fuzzing
Framework, highlighting its implementation in Python and C++ for optimal performance in
concurrent software environments.</jats:p>

title: Effectiveness of a hybrid Machine Learning Model for War Against Money Laundering in Nigeria

affiliation.name: Computer Science Department, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, Anambra State

journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>This paper examined the effectiveness of machine learning (ML) Models for the ongoing war
against money laundering in Nigeria. In advanced economies, the rise of machine learning has
revolutionized the way financial institutions and governments combat illegal financial activities
emanating from mobile money transactions. By using advanced algorithms and data analysis
techniques, machine learning has proven to be an effective tool in identifying suspicious financial
transactions and patterns, thereby helping authorities take proactive rather than reactive
measures in preventing fraudulent transactions. This study aimed to address the research gap in
the use of reactive approach by Nigeria government, where the prevalence of money laundering
has risen in recent years, and explored how ML techniques can be utilized to enhance the country’s
efforts in combating this financial crime.The datasets for this study were obtained from Kaggle
website that contains fraudulent transactions on money laundering, which was used to train,
validate and test the ML models. Logistic regression (LR) and Support Vector Machine (SVM)
were used as the baseline models while Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) neural network was used for
feature learning and dimensionality reduction. The results indicate that LR classifier still showed
reasonable performance but did not outperform the other models. Among all the measures, SVM
exhibited outstanding performance, with over 90% prediction accuracy. The amount of money
transferred and location of transactions emerged as top features for predicting money laundering
transactions in online money transfers. These findings suggest that further research is needed to
enhance the logistic regression model, and sparse autoencoder neural network should be explored
as potential tool for law enforcement agencies and Nigeria financial Institutions to proactively
learn representative data from high dimensional datasets as quality of data improves performance
of predictive models.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>The practical challenge posed by corporate bankruptcy prediction does not stem from the limitations of any particular classifier but rather from the very structure of the data. Financial datasets are typically plagued by numerous missing values, cluttered with partially redundant ratios, and structurally imbalanced, with failing firms representing only a small minority of observations. This paper proposes DAWN (Directional Asymmetry-Weighted dissimilarity for Nearest-case retrieval), a novel framework resting on four pillars: (i) Missing values are imputed using Case-Based Reasoning (CBR), where the nearest donor case is identified according to the proposed DAWN dissimilarity measure rather than conventional Euclidean, Manhattan, or cosine distances. (ii) Feature selection is performed using DAWN-FS, which ranks variables through a hybrid criterion combining mutual information with directional discriminability, retaining variables only when their class-specific medians exhibit the empirically identified direction of association with financial distress. (iii) Class imbalance is addressed using DAWN-SMOTE, an oversampling strategy that constructs minority-class neighborhoods according to the DAWN dissimilarity measure and introduces a directional interpolation mechanism that, on a ratio-specific basis, biases synthetic samples toward the identified risk trajectory. (iv) The SVM hyperparameters are optimized using a hybrid Open Competency Optimization–Particle Swarm Optimization (OCO–PSO) metaheuristic, guided by a G-mean-based fitness function. The proposed DAWN-SVM framework is evaluated as an integrated end-to-end methodology against baseline pipelines on one real-world UK dataset and three public benchmarks (Taiwan, Russian, and Slovak), using stratified 10-fold cross-validation across nine metrics, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Holm–Bonferroni correction. All preprocessing parameters, including CBR-DAWN imputation, are estimated within each training fold to prevent data leakage. The four pillars are designed to operate jointly within one prediction pipeline, sharing the same robust scale, risk direction, and informational weight; the performance claims in this paper therefore concern the complete DAWN-SVM framework. DAWN-SVM ranks first on all nine metrics, with 27 of the 36 comparisons against the baselines remaining significant after Holm–Bonferroni correction and none favoring a baseline. The improvements are particularly pronounced on the dataset with the most missing values and on the severely imbalanced Russian dataset. These end-to-end results support the effectiveness of the integrated framework under challenging missing-data and class-imbalance conditions. A dedicated analysis of the dissimilarity itself shows that DAWN retrieves firms with the same outcome more accurately than the Euclidean, Manhattan, and cosine measures and that this advantage is robust to the number of ratios and to the strength of the directional penalty.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>This study proposed numerical techniques in the mesh‐free Moving Particle Semi‐implicit (MPS) method to improve pressure field calculation in granular flows. The Explicit Incompressible scheme in the MPS (EI‐MPS) method is employed to solve the pressure Poisson equation, and a re‐corrector time step is further incorporated to update the pressure field. The improved EI‐MPS method is used to simulate granular column collapses, the collision of two granular columns, and a sand impact flow. It is found that the obtained pressure field in the flows is very smooth, and the velocity and free surface variations are reproduced by the numerical method. The effect of the re‐corrector technique is examined, and it can be beneficial to eliminate pressure noise close to the free surface by using the improved EI‐MPS method.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We have demonstrated laser induced fluorescence in a capacitively coupled plasma discharge to measure the most crucial ion properties at a discharge regime suitable for a broad range of plasma research related to plasma processing and dusty plasma investigations that has been impossible for many years. The ion flow measurements in the presence and absence of dust particles show that ions move much faster directionally than expected from thermal motion, with reductions observed in the presence of dust particles. Ion temperatures are also found to exceed room temperature, contrary to a common assumption in the dusty plasma community. These findings represent a significant advancement in experimental plasma research, providing vital information to refine ion-driven process models with insights that span multiple research fields.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Infected wounds, particularly those caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), often result in dysfunctional healing and fibrotic scarring. This study investigates whether a flexible dielectric barrier discharge cold atmospheric plasma (DBD-CAP) device improves healing quality in MRSA-infected murine full-thickness wounds. Mice were treated with DBD-CAP for 2 min every 48 h, and wound tissues were assessed at days 3, 7, 14, and 21. DBD-CAP treatment significantly reduced bacterial burden and inflammatory infiltration without altering macroscopic closure kinetics. In this improved microenvironment, histological analysis revealed restored basal-restricted integrin α5 polarity and ordered Ki-67 proliferation, indicating a higher quality of re-epithelialization. DBD-CAP also resulted in early angiogenesis at day 7, followed by vascular remodeling at day 14, and led to a lower collagen I/III ratio, smaller scars, and hair regrowth by day 21. Infrared thermography confirmed absence of significant thermal elevation, and repeated exposure showed no systemic toxicity. These results suggest that resolving infection with DBD-CAP creates a favorable microenvironment associated with high-quality, anti-fibrotic tissue repair, independent of accelerated closure speed. While the current experimental design cannot isolate whether these benefits are a direct regenerative effect of the plasma or a secondary, natural healing process resulting from bacterial clearance, this study provides phenotypic evidence for plasma-based wound therapy.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Background: Plasma medicine has emerged as a promising approach for cancer treatment, with reactive oxygen and nitrogen species generated by plasma contributing to cellular stress and tumor cell death. However, the effects of plasma treatment on membrane transporter regulation remain poorly understood. Methods: This study investigated whether plasma exposure alters the gene expression of pharmacologically and biologically relevant transporters across diverse cancer cell lines, and whether these responses are conserved in an in ovo tumor model. Twelve cancer cell lines representing squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, and adenocarcinoma were treated with plasma at cell line-specific IC25 conditions. The expression of ten transporter genes was assessed by targeted quantitative PCR. Results: Plasma treatment induced heterogeneous changes in transporter gene expression, with both up- and downregulation observed across cell lines and transporters. SLC2A2, ABCC2, SLCO3A1, and SLC28A3 displayed particularly pronounced and distinct response patterns. Correlation analysis further identified coordinated changes among several transporter genes, suggesting shared response patterns to plasma-induced stress. Selected transporter responses were subsequently assessed in an in ovo tumor model, revealing partial conservation of plasma-induced transcriptional regulation alongside substantial context-dependent differences in response magnitude and direction. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that plasma treatment can modulate transporter gene expression in a heterogeneous and cell line-dependent manner. The observed regulation may reflect broader cellular adaptations to plasma-induced stress and could have implications for cellular drug handling and pharmacological response.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With the development of inertial confinement fusion facilities, the surface cleanliness of key optical components has become increasingly important for stable system operation. Conventional cleaning methods can remove organic contaminants to some extent, but residual control, secondary contamination, and process compatibility may still be challenging in ultra‐clean optical applications. Low‐pressure plasma cleaning offers low‐residue processing and reduced risk of secondary contamination. However, the cleaning mechanism and process regularities of plasma cleaning for fused silica optical components remain insufficiently understood, and systematic optimization of process parameters is still limited. Using dibutyl phthalate (DBP) as a representative organic contaminant, this study systematically investigates the adsorption behavior of DBP on fused silica, its decomposition mechanism under low‐pressure oxygen plasma, and the effects of cleaning time and power on cleaning effectiveness, thereby providing a basis for optimizing low‐pressure plasma cleaning processes. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the physical adsorption of organic contaminants on fused silica, and white‐light interferometry was employed to characterize the surface morphology of fused silica components under different contamination states. Single‐factor and full‐factorial experiments were further conducted to evaluate the effects of cleaning time and power on contaminant removal, followed by optimization of these process parameters using response surface methodology. The results clarify the reaction pathway for DBP decomposition during low‐pressure plasma cleaning and identify reasonable cleaning parameters through process optimization, providing theoretical support and experimental data for low‐pressure plasma cleaning of ultra‐clean optical components.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>The output performance of photovoltaic modules with cell-level total cross-tied (TCT) interconnection was compared with that of simple series-parallel (SP) modules under partial shading conditions. In the SP module, partial shading reduced the short-circuit current, resulting in a significant decrease in output power. In addition, hot spots were observed in several cells. Although the TCT module exhibited a similar reduction in the short-circuit current, the output power loss was smaller because of an improved fill factor. The experimental results demonstrate that TCT cell interconnection effectively suppresses hot spot formation under partial shading conditions. Circuit simulations reproduced the experimental results and enabled prediction of the cell temperature rise under partial shading conditions.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>There are few therapeutic options to treat patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), a blood disorder caused by mutations in the β-globin gene that affects > 7M individuals worldwide. Combining human genetics and high-throughput proteomics can help identify new drug targets. Here, we present results from a proteogenomic analysis of the plasma proteome in SCD patients. We measured the levels of 5,411 plasma proteins and tested their associations with common genetic variation in 343 SCD patients. After conditional analyses, we identified 560 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), including 58 (10%) that are novel. Many of these pQTL are not specific to SCD patients and associate with clinically relevant traits in non-SCD African Americans from the Million Veteran Program (e.g., hemoglobin concentration, triglycerides). The effect sizes of the pQTL are largely concordant between SCD and non-SCD individuals, although we found examples (e.g., APOL1, haptoglobin) with evidence of heterogeneity that suggests an interaction between the plasma proteome and the SCD genotype. Finally, we combine pQTL and genome-wide association study results for fetal hemoglobin (HbF) in a Mendelian randomization analysis to prioritize four proteins that may increase HbF production (ENPP5, LBP, PTX3, ZP3). We have combined high-throughput DNA genotyping and plasma proteome profiling to confirm known and identify new genetic variants associated with protein level variation in SCD. Our results provide an opportunity to prioritize novel SCD drug targets that are informed by human genetics.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate the potential causal relationships between circulating plasma proteins and non-small cell lung cancer and to assess whether antibody immune response traits mediate these associations.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted an integrative genetic epidemiology study combining two-sample Mendelian randomization, mediation analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, and tissue-based experimental validation. Plasma protein data for 4907 proteins and genome-wide association study summary statistics for 46 antibody immune response traits were analyzed alongside non-small cell lung cancer genome-wide association study data from 218,792 individuals of European ancestry (1627 cases and 217,165 controls). Five complementary Mendelian randomization methods were applied; sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, and robustness, and reverse Mendelian randomization assessed potential reverse causation. Mediation analysis evaluated antibody immune response traits as candidate intermediate phenotypes. Prioritized proteins were further characterized using single-cell RNA sequencing data and paired tumor and adjacent normal tissues from patients with histopathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We identified 1188 plasma proteins with potential causal associations with non-small cell lung cancer risk. CLEC10A and TGM3 were prioritized through sequential plasma protein–non-small cell lung cancer, plasma protein–antibody immune response, and mediation analyses. Higher genetically predicted CLEC10A levels were associated with increased non-small cell lung cancer risk, whereas higher genetically predicted TGM3 levels were associated with lower non-small cell lung cancer risk. Five antibody immune response traits were initially associated with non-small cell lung cancer, of which four were retained after robustness assessment. Mediation analysis identified three candidate plasma protein–antibody immune response–non-small cell lung cancer pathways involving GCST90006921 and GCST90006923. Single-cell analysis localized CLEC10A and TGM3 predominantly to macrophages, while paired tissue analyses showed higher CLEC10A and lower TGM3 expression in tumors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CLEC10A and TGM3 may contribute to non-small cell lung cancer susceptibility, with specific antibody immune response traits representing candidate intermediate immune pathways. These findings provide genetic and complementary biological support for further independent replication and mechanistic investigation.</jats:p>

title: Interprofessional simulation-based training for obstetric and neonatal emergencies: a systematic review
abstract:
<jats:p>Background</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Co-ordinated multidisciplinary response is essential in managing delivery room emergencies, though many current simulation initiatives remain single-profession or focus on separate care streams. While interprofessional simulation-based training (IP SBT) programmes have been increasingly adopted to improve team performance, this systematic review provides the first global evaluation of its prevalence, structure and effectiveness across Kirkpatrick-level outcomes. By examining participant perceptions, clinical knowledge and patient/organization-level outcomes, this review identifies critical structural gaps to guide the future development of integrated maternal-neonatal emergency programmes.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Methods</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Systematic search and data extraction followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 7473 studies were identified through PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL and MEDLINE databases (updated March 2026). Forty studies from 18 countries fulfilled inclusion criteria. All included simulation of both obstetric and neonatal emergencies involving at least two healthcare professions. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and JBI tools, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE criteria.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Results</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Programmes varied in structure and high-technology use, with postpartum haemorrhage (n = 27), shoulder dystocia (n = 25) and neonatal resuscitation (n = 22) being the most frequently simulated scenarios. Only 12.5% of studies (n = 5) specifically simulated concurrent maternal-neonatal emergencies requiring simultaneous resuscitation. Outcome synthesis using the Kirkpatrick hierarchy demonstrated widespread improvements in participant reactions (n = 17), clinical knowledge (n = 23) and teamwork/communication behaviours (n = 15). Organizational outcomes (n = 7) included identification of latent safety threats and equipment preparedness, whilst patient-level outcomes included a 21% reduction in Caesarean section rates and up to a 34% decrease in neonatal mortality and intrapartum stillbirth. The overall certainty of evidence was moderate.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Conclusion</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Limited, heterogeneous evidence suggests that IP SBT for delivery room emergencies positively influenced team performance and clinical proficiency. This review identifies a major structural gap in simulation design, with only 12.5% (n = 5) simulating the concurrent resuscitation of both mother and newborn. While widespread improvements were noted in teamwork, communication and clinical knowledge, evidence linking simulation to sustained clinical translation and patient outcomes remains sparse. Future research should investigate optimal scenario sequencing (simultaneous vs. sequential), evaluate the effectiveness of emerging online and blended delivery models, and focus on longitudinal evaluation of patient-level impacts.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A growth mindset refers to the belief that abilities and intelligence can be developed through effort, learning, and persistence. Although digital games are often associated with motivational and learning benefits, little is known about how they are intentionally designed to foster growth mindset in preK–12 learners. Understanding how growth mindset principles are operationalized within game mechanics and learning environments is critical for advancing both theory and practice in serious game design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This systematic review synthesizes how digital games have been designed and implemented to promote growth mindset in preK–12 education and examines associated student outcomes and future research directions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Following PRISMA guidelines, we screened 2,063 records across multiple databases and included 12 empirical studies that explicitly integrated growth-mindset-supportive design elements into digital games. Data were extracted and analyzed to identify trends in study design, targeted competencies, reported effects, and specific game design features.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Most reviewed studies reported positive effects on growth mindset and related competencies (e.g., persistence, creativity, self-efficacy), although some showed mixed or non-significant effects linked to design quality or implementation context. Two overarching design categories emerged: direct supports (e.g., explicit mindset instruction and effort-based rewards) and indirect supports (e.g., adaptive challenges, scaffolding, and mastery-oriented gameplay).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Well-designed digital games hold promise for fostering growth mindset in preK–12 contexts. However, the evidence base remains limited, highlighting the need for more rigorous research designs, longer-term interventions, and deeper theoretical integration to inform scalable and effective game-based mindset interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The use of microparticles for high-cell-density cultures has been extensively studied. While various polymers have been used for microparticle preparation, each polymer differs, and a unique methodology for fabrication and surface modification is needed. In this context, we present a systematic approach to developing a polymer microparticle system for protein expression. This approach starts with understanding PDMS and plasma polymerization in two-dimensional (2D) to assess their compatibility for HEK293 and Sf9 insect cells. To transition to three-dimensional (3D), we optimized a three-step plasma polymerization process to overcome shadowing during deposition on spherical geometries. Finally, we validated plasma-polymerized 3D PDMS microparticles for protein expression using Sf9 insect cells. This framework provides a robust template for developing and implementing a microparticle and a coating method for recombinant protein expression.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Scenario-based high-fidelity simulation has been increasingly used in medical education, yet its role in assessing general practice residents’ emergency competencies after emergency department rotation remains under-explored.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Eighty-two general practice resident physicians were selected as study subjects. Both upon entering and exiting the emergency department, they were assessed to direct a team to perform CPR under scenario simulation conditions. The assessments compared various factors( Table 1). The subjects were divided into two groups: a resuscitation room rotation group (45) and a non-resuscitation room rotation group (37). The total CPR assessment scores upon entering and exiting the department were compared between the two groups. The number of resuscitations each participant had attended during the rotation was recorded.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The scores for the judgment of the condition before CA, rescue measures for CA,, uninterrupted compressions, timing of defibrillation, treatment after ROSC, humanistic care, teamwork, and overall assessment were significantly lower upon entering the department compared to exiting the department. There were no significant differences in airway management, chest compressions, and defibrillation (energy selection, defibrillation position). The overall scores for the resuscitation room rotation group were higher upon exiting the department compared to the non-resuscitation room rotation group (Cohen’s d = 3.29, 95%CI 8.65–11.32,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001), but there was no difference upon entering the department (Cohen’s d = -0.01, 95%CI -1.93-1.85,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.97). Both the resuscitation room group and the non-resuscitation room group demonstrated significant improvement in total scores from entry to exit (Cohen’s d = 3.93, 95%CI 17.46–20.36, Cohen’s d = 2.35, 95%CI 7.62–10.15, both
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). ROC analysis identified 8.5 resuscitations as the optimal cut-off for predicting excellent performance (AUC = 0.785,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Scenario-Based High-Fidelity Simulation effectively captures the improvement in emergency care competencies of general practice residents following their emergency department rotation, supporting its utility as a valuable assessment tool.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract: <jats:p>Inflammatory responses involve dynamic interactions among circulating immune and non-immune cells, including neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets. Peripheral blood cell-derived inflammatory indices, particularly the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), have gained increasing attention as readily accessible composite markers of systemic inflammatory and immune alterations. Growing evidence links these indices with disease severity, treatment response, and clinical outcomes across cardiovascular, malignant, autoimmune, infectious, and metabolic diseases. However, their translation into routine clinical practice remains limited by the absence of robust, externally validated, and transferable cut-off values. Reported thresholds vary substantially according to disease type and stage, patient characteristics, clinical endpoints, preanalytical and analytical conditions, and the statistical approaches used for cut-off derivation. This narrative review draws on English-language literature identified through searches of PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar conducted between March 18 and October 19, 2026, with publications selected for their relevance to the biological basis, clinical applications, and methodological challenges of peripheral blood cell-derived inflammatory indices. It examines the biological basis of these indices, with particular emphasis on relevant cellular interactions and inflammatory signaling pathways, summarizes current evidence across major disease categories, and critically evaluates the biological, clinical, analytical, and methodological factors contributing to cut-off variability and limiting the establishment of reliable clinical decision thresholds. We further consider whether universal cut-off values are biologically and clinically justified and propose that context-specific, endpoint-specific, and externally validated thresholds may provide a more appropriate framework for clinical implementation.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>Angesichts der weitreichenden technischen Entwicklung sprachverarbeitender Systeme erscheint es auch aus theoretischer Sicht wichtig, (fachliche) Kommunikation zwischen Künstlicher Intelligenz selbst zu modellieren, um die Merkmale dieser Interaktion besser einschätzen zu können.
