abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We study circular orbits of charged particles around a Schwarzschild black hole threaded by the magnetic field of a smooth finite-width equatorial current distribution. We construct an axis-regular source, retain both algebraic circular-orbit branches, and fix the coupling sign through the distant-loop limit, in which strong positive coupling drives the inner marginally stable orbit toward the horizon. We map orbit existence, radial stability, vertical stability, and bound-orbit status for both coupling signs. For positive coupling, radially stable equatorial orbits may separate into an inner band and a detached outer band, with a radial-instability gap between them. For negative coupling, the corresponding separation is produced mainly by loss of an admissible positive-angular-momentum orbit. We also identify stable off-equatorial circular-orbit families. Convergence tests and direct integration verify the principal boundaries. A regular current source can therefore reorganize the circular-orbit structure rather than merely shift the Schwarzschild innermost stable orbit.</jats:p>

title: A theory of spatial simulation in video games: Selective realism and the production of virtual territory
abstract: <jats:p>Video games have become one of the dominant media through which space is experienced, imagined, and learned, yet no general framework accounts for how they simulate territory as an operational system rather than merely as an image. The aim of this article is to explain a recurring pattern: video games distribute geographical fidelity unevenly, enhancing features that support visual clarity, emotional engagement, and playability, while compressing or omitting dynamic processes, systemic interdependencies, and socio-spatial complexity. To this end, a geographical theory of virtual territory production is proposed, structured around four analytical dimensions and six recurring design operations. The guiding concept is selective realism. Originally used in game studies to describe experiential filtering (Pötzsch 2017), the term is redirected here toward territorial analysis to capture this uneven distribution of geographical fidelity across the different layers of simulated environment. Drawing on a comparative synthesis of empirical analyses across open-world, coastal, and urban simulation games, the article develops four analytical dimensions of spatial simulation (morphological, functional, semantic, and political) and identifies six recurring operations through which selective realism is materialised. The resulting virtual territories are aesthetically compelling and functionally coherent, but their patterns of simplification carry epistemological and ideological consequences that warrant critical geographical attention.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Intratumor heterogeneity (ITH) contributes to treatment resistance and poor outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its cellular basis and prognostic relevance remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to develop an ITH-centered prognostic framework by integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We integrated bulk transcriptomes from 363 TCGA-LIHC tumors with single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE149614. DEPTH2 was used to quantify ITH, and Scissor analysis mapped the high-ITH phenotype onto single-cell populations. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting ITH-associated, disease-associated, and key cell population-associated differentially expressed genes, followed by univariate Cox regression and a 101-combination machine-learning pipeline. A five-gene random survival forest (RSF) signature was constructed and evaluated in the independent GSE14520 cohort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>High ITH was associated with shorter overall survival, and Scissor localized the high-ITH signal predominantly to macrophages. The final five-gene RSF signature (FABP5, PKM, HPX, TAT, and HRG) achieved an apparent C-index of 0.771 (95% CI: 0.733–0.810) in the training cohort and was validated in the independent GSE14520 cohort (C-index = 0.636, 95% CI: 0.574–0.698), with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs of 0.670, 0.671, and 0.681 in external validation. The risk score remained independently associated with survival after clinical adjustment, and a risk score-stage nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.778 (95% CI: 0.737–0.818). High-risk tumors showed greater copy-number burden, distinct pathway activity, increased immune checkpoint expression, stronger predicted immune evasion, and differential predicted drug sensitivity. Human Protein Atlas data supported the expression and prognostic patterns of the five genes, and qRT-PCR in five paired clinical specimens confirmed their expected tumor expression changes. Molecular docking nominated tranilast as a candidate PKM-binding compound, although a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation indicated an unstable binding pose.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings support an ITH-associated, macrophage-linked five-gene framework for HCC risk stratification and provide cautious, testable hypotheses for biomarker-guided therapeutic investigation. Larger multicenter prospective cohorts and mechanistic experiments are needed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>Summary</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Evaluation of hydraulic-fracture geometry is crucial for enhancing production in unconventional shale-oil reservoirs, and electrical responses near energized steel-cased wells provide significant potential for fracture monitoring. In this study, we systematically evaluate the practical feasibility and controlling factors of hydraulic-fracture detection using direct-current (DC) resistivity in steel-cased wells. A finite element approach is used to construct 3D geoelectric models of complex fractures and steel-cased wells. Surface-, casing-, and borehole-based monitoring configurations are considered under different source, fracture, casing, and formation conditions. The numerical results demonstrate that source location strongly controls fracture detectability, with a positive electrode placed inside the steel-cased well significantly enhancing fracture monitoring, and casing- and borehole-based measurements providing higher detectability than surface measurements. The results further show that the monitoring signal depends mainly on the volume of high-conductivity proppant and the contact area between the fracture and the steel-cased well, rather than fracture shape alone. Casing corrosion substantially reduces fracture signals, but additional electrodes between the damaged section and the fractured zone improve fracture detectability, with an electrode spacing of approximately 5–10 m yielding favorable responses. Anomalous bodies affect monitoring by diverting current through the surrounding formation, while high-resistivity anomalies have a comparatively limited impact. The method remains effective under multiborehole and multistage fracturing conditions. These results identify the key factors controlling fracture detectability and provide quantitative guidance for selecting source and measurement configurations for hydraulic fracture monitoring in steel-cased wells.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine the proportional fidelity of software-generated digital avatars and how proportional deviations affect virtual garment fit in 3D simulation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Five matched pairs of standard anthropometric and software-generated avatars were compared under identical simulation conditions, using a women’s trouser prototype (size 38). Proportional differences were quantified with a newly developed Weighted Proportional Deviation Index (PDIw) and Bland–Altman analysis, applied descriptively as a proof of concept.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Software-generated avatars generally preserve global stature scaling but exhibit systematic proportional distortions in lower-limb dimensions, particularly knee circumference and relative trouser length.                   <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study covers a single garment type and five matched avatar pairs, so the findings are exploratory and no inferential claims are made. <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD), capable of sustaining non-thermal plasmas at atmospheric pressure, shows great potential for many emerging applications. This paper presents a tutorial demonstration of fundamental plasma parameters in DBDs based on the one-dimensional fluid model with Local-Mean-Energy Approximation. The model incorporates the electron density and energy balance equations coupled with Poisson’s equation, and its accuracy has been verified by comparison with experimental results. The validated model was subsequently utilized to investigate detailed DBD characteristics, encompassing discharge current, gap voltage dynamics, charge accumulation on dielectric surfaces, Lissajous figures for power calculation, and discharge symmetry. The transition of the discharge from the symmetric single-period (SP1) to the asymmetric single-period (AP1) mode is analyzed, and the formulation for the gap voltage components is derived. This work is designed to serve as a practical guide for practitioners to computational plasma discharge simulations.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We study the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of a charged particle around a Kerr black hole in the electromagnetic field of an equatorial current loop. The field is treated as a test field. We apply the relativistic precession model to the three simultaneous quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) of GRO J1655–40. Neutral Kerr motion reproduces the QPO frequencies and the black-hole mass measured from the companion-star orbit, but it gives a spin lower than the value obtained from fitting the thermal x-ray spectrum. In the outer dipole approximation, the three QPO frequencies can be reproduced with a mass consistent with the companion-star measurement and a spin consistent with that inferred from fitting the thermal x-ray spectrum. At leading order, the result already depends on whether the particle orbit lies inside or outside the loop; higher multipoles introduce an additional strong dependence on the loop radius. For the sampled solutions, the fitted mass remains closest to the dynamical estimate when the particle orbit lies outside a compact loop, whereas an orbit inside the loop gives larger masses.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>The preference for high-fat diets has increased the risk of developing cardio-metabolic metabolic
disorders. The aim of this study was to examine the effect of Justicia carnea (JC) leaf extract on
plasma and fecal lipid profile [total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), high density lipoprotein
(HDL), low density lipoprotein (LDL)] in high-fat diet fed wistar rats. The study involved a total
of thirty wistar rats separated into six groups of five rats each. Group 1 served as control while
groups 2 to 6 were fed with high-fat diet (HFD) throughout the period of the experiment. Group 2
remained untreated, Groups 3, 4 and 5 received respectively 200mg/kg, 500mg/kg and 1000mg/kg
of JC extract. Group 6 received 10mg/kg of simvastatin. The animals were fed with the extract for
twenty-eight days and thereafter plasma and fecal samples were collected to determine the lipid
profile. Daily administration of 200mg/kg of JC caused a significant reduction in the plasma levels
of total cholesterol (TC) but significant increase in fecal total cholesterol (FTC). The higher doses
also showed a similar pattern but not significantly. Administration of 500mg/kg of JC caused
significant increase in plasma TG and HDL compared to the HFD only group. All three doses of
JC caused significant reduction in LDL. Conclusively, the results from the present study suggest
that JC could possess plasma lipid lowering property and also enhanced fecal excretion of
cholesterol. This effect could be possibly due to decreased absorption of lipids and increased fecal
excretion of lipids.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>Nesprins form a diverse family of nuclear envelope scaffold proteins. Canonical Nesprin isoforms link the nuclear envelope to cytoskeletal networks through SUN–KASH interactions in the linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) complex. Through these connections, Nesprins shape nuclear positioning, organize the perinuclear cytoskeleton, transmit mechanical forces, and support nuclear envelope homeostasis.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Scope</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This review examines canonical Nesprin isoforms in skeletal muscle fibers and cardiomyocytes. Rather than treating Nesprins only at the gene level, we emphasize differences among isoforms in domain architecture, subcellular localization, binding partners, and cellular functions.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Key themes</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Isoform diversity is especially relevant in striated muscle, where nuclei constantly experience mechanical stress. We discuss how canonical Nesprin isoforms contribute to nuclear organization, cytoskeletal linkage, mechanotransduction, and muscle dysfunction in skeletal and cardiac muscle.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Perspective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An isoform-centered view offers a more precise way to understand Nesprin function in muscle cells. It also helps explain how disrupted nucleo-cytoskeletal coupling may contribute to muscle disease.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Electrically conductive composite ceramics face a critical trade-off where increasing the phase domain size ratio between the insulating matrix and the conductive phase theoretically enhances conductivity but practically hinders densification. The resulting porosity inevitably degrades both mechanical and electrical properties. To address this limitation, a matrix particle size grading strategy is proposed using the Al2O3–TiC system as a model. The incorporation of nano-Al2O3 into a micro-Al2O3 matrix triggers a synergistic microstructural evolution. Specifically, nano-Al2O3 particles fill interparticle spaces to promote densification and may pin TiC grain boundaries, thereby contributing to the refinement of the conductive phase domains. Concurrently, the micro-Al2O3 phase domains coarsen at the expense of nano-Al2O3, maximizing the phase domain size disparity and favoring the formation of a continuous three-dimensional (3D) TiC network. With 10 vol% nano-Al2O3 addition, the calculated effective percolation threshold drops from 15.54 vol% to 10.20 vol%, achieving an electrical conductivity of 4.02×104 S/m. Consequently, the composite exhibits enhanced electrical discharge machining (EDM) performance, achieving a material removal rate (MRR) of 9.50 mm2/min alongside high surface quality. This strategy offers a robust framework for developing advanced conductive ceramics tailored for EDM applications.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>The analysis of stable isotopes has emerged as a pivotal method in paleodietary reconstruction. However, existing methodologies for isotopic data analysis often rely on manual processes that are particularly time-consuming. To address this, we developed SALEM, a standalone, user-friendly application designed to streamline isotopic data processing. The current version of SALEM is tailored for analyses of bone and dentine collagen, focusing on dietary and weaning reconstructions using carbon, nitrogen, and sulphur isotopes. The application is organized into distinct tabs that guide researchers through essential steps, including quality control, analytical uncertainty assessment, statistical analysis and explanation, and data visualization. Additionally, SALEM integrates established statistical methods for weaning reconstruction, allowing researchers to apply them directly without external coding or tools. We applied SALEM to six published datasets, demonstrating its capacity to manage and interpret complex isotopic data in bioarchaeological research. The development of SALEM responds to the growing need for a centralized and efficient platform for isotopic data analysis. This application is particularly beneficial for researchers, enabling them to analyse isotopic data without requiring extensive programming expertise. While currently focused on collagen-based studies of subadult and adult diet reconstructions, future versions aim to broaden its analytical capabilities across a wider range of tissues and research questions. We envision SALEM evolving into a versatile platform supporting diverse isotopic applications in archaeology and beyond.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>This study presents a comprehensive mercury (Hg) isotope dataset for Australian lignite and bituminous coals and examines isotope behaviour during the lignite combustion. Australian coals extend the global isotopic range towards more negative Δ199Hg values, while preserving the global mass-independent fractionation (MIF) relationship. abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The very high-energy (E &gt; 100 GeV) afterglow emission in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) can be explained by synchrotron self-Compton (SSC). Modeling this emission accurately requires fully numerical codes that solve the time-dependent coupled particle–photon kinetic equations while accounting for Klein–Nishina suppression. However, their substantial computational cost makes them impractical for traditional parameter inference techniques such as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. In this work, we present a highly efficient surrogate model based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) that emulates a one-zone kinetic SSC radiation code. To train our ANN, we use a multi-dimensional model parameter grid that constitutes a sample of 100,800 spectra produced by an infinitely thin spherical blast wave propagating inside a constant density interstellar medium (ISM). The ANN reproduces the numerical spectra well, with the median relative error generally below 2 per cent across the full frequency domain. Using this surrogate framework, we perform Bayesian parameter posterior estimation via MCMC and fit the broadband GRB afterglow observations of GRB 190114C from X-rays to TeV γ-rays at different epochs. We find an energetic jet with isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of Ek, iso ≃ 7.2 × 1054 erg moving with a coasting bulk Lorentz factor of Γ ≳ 500 into an ISM with density n ≃ 0.1 cm−3. The deviation of our model light curve from observations on long timescales suggests that an ISM environment is inconsistent, and instead favours a radially stratified external medium.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Magnetoresistance oscillations under microwave (3–300 GHz) and terahertz (300 GHz–10 THz) excitation are well-established phenomena in high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron systems. Here, we report a distinct class of photoinduced magnetoresistance oscillations under very-high-frequency (VHF) and ultra-high-frequency (UHF) excitation below 1 GHz. The observed oscillations are periodic in inverse magnetic field, while the oscillation period varies systematically with the applied rf source power. Comparison with conventional microwave-induced magnetoresistance oscillations indicates that the first observable oscillatory peak corresponds to P2, suggesting the absence of the principal oscillatory peak P1. Analysis of the Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations further reveals concomitant electron heating under VHF and UHF excitation. These observations identify a distinct low-frequency photoinduced magnetotransport regime in high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron systems.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Constrained transmission corridors motivate comparison of high‐temperature superconducting high‐voltage direct‐current (HTS‐HVDC) with conventional VSC‐HVDC under a common receiving‐end service and contingency requirement. This study links three questions: how transmission ratings determine installed reserve, how much additional conventional corridor capital is required for parity and what conductor procurement price permits parity. The calculation purchases complete cable, converter and cooling inventories for independent modules and evaluates lifecycle expenditure and delivered energy. A 2‐GW conventional reference is compared with 2‐, 3‐, 4‐ and 5‐GW HTS planning modules using a common converter–cost relationship. At 2.1 GW receiving‐end power and 500 km, the additional conventional capital required for parity is approximately USD 0.80 billion for equal‐2‐GW modules and USD 1.39 billion for 5‐GW HTS modules. Fewer HTS assemblies can therefore coincide with a higher cost of installed reserve. Conductor‐price thresholds depend on that architecture and the assumed additional‐corridor capital; three heat‐ingress scenarios show their thermal sensitivity. Reliability and input uncertainty qualify these conditions rather than establish commercial feasibility. The calculations use published component correlations and explicit author cost and reliability scenarios. Historical project comparisons do not validate the conventional coefficients, and conductor‐current evidence does not qualify a complete 5‐GW cable system. The outputs are architecture‐specific conditions for further engineering and project appraisal, not estimates of demonstrated avoided corridor expenditure.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>It has been 40 years since high-temperature superconductivity (HTSC) in cuprates was discovered. Despite initial optimism, the microscopic origin of this remarkable phenomenon remains unknown.                   <jats:p>Cyanated amides, α-cyano amides and α-amino nitriles, are highly desirable motifs and valuable synthons owing to their important roles in chemical synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Conventional approaches to these compounds typically rely on the nucleophilic attack of cyanide on imines (iminium ions) or on radical transformations from prefunctionalized alkyl halides, respectively. Herein, we report a ligand-free, copper-catalyzed cyanation reaction that enables the preparation of both classes of compounds via direct C−H functionalization without light. This method harnesses the strongly reducing carbon dioxide radical anion, aryl-radical-mediated intramolecular 1,5-HAT, and Cu-catalyzed aliphatic cyanation, featuring an efficient sequence of ET/HAT events. The reaction operates simply under mild conditions, employs inexpensive commercial reagents, exhibits broad functional group compatibility and can be applied to functionalize natural products and bioactive molecules with good yields.</jats:p>

title: Golden economy and agriculture – Renewable energy or digitalisation and high-tech innovation
abstract: <jats:p>Sustainable and resilient agricultural systems play a key role in global growth and development. In the context of globalisation and Industry 5.0, the concept of "golden economy" is viewed from two perspectives. On the one hand, it is linked to the development of the use of renewable sources, and on the other, it is associated with digitalisation, innovation, and artificial intelligence. This study aims to analyse how the elements of the golden economy, namely renewable energy, digitalisation, and innovation, impact agriculture and to identify the challenges facing the sector. The connections between the individual elements have been deduced. An analysis of the cost-effectiveness of golden economy and its impact on agriculture has been made. The results obtained show that new and emerging technologies and their applications in the agricultural sector have the potential to impact multiple aspects of farming, including new business models and product designs, competition, operational efficiency and accessibility.</jats:p>

title: Multi-objective energy optimization in intelligent grids with high renewable penetration
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As renewable energy sources enter into smart grids, the intermittency, uncertainty, storage coordination, operational cost, carbon emissions and stability of these grids will pose significant challenges. Optimization techniques in conventional systems or rule-based energy management systems are not able to adapt to the fast changes of operating conditions continuously. This paper proposes a Multi-Objective Adaptive Deep Reinforcement Learning (MO-ADRL) framework for real-time optimization of energy in the intelligent grid with high renewable energy penetration. Energy management is formulated as a sequential decision-making problem, and an actor–critic deep reinforcement learning architecture computes continuous dispatch actions. The agent has a Temporal Transformer module which forecasts short-term electricity demand and renewable generation to make proactive decisions. The algorithm contains an adaptive multi-objective reward mechanism which dynamically balances the operational cost, carbon emission, utilization of renewable energy, renewable curtailment, peak demand, battery degradation, and energy supply reliability. Prioritized experience replay is integrated so that transitions with large temporal-difference errors, which usually correspond to critical grid events, are revisited more often during training. The proposed framework achieves real time coordination of solar PV, wind, battery energy storage, grid electricity and flexible demand. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms rule-based energy management, PSO, GA, DQN, DDPG, PPO and SAC for renewable penetration levels from 40% to 80%. At 80% penetration, MO-ADRL lowers the daily operating cost by 31.11% and CO₂ emissions by 38.09% relative to rule-based management, raises renewable utilization to 96.8%, reduces peak demand by 33.76% and keeps supply reliability at 99.6%. MO-ADRL therefore offers an adaptive and scalable route to autonomous energy management in future renewable-dominated intelligent grids.</jats:p>

The thermochromic coating provides a direct optical indication of sudden temperature increase, as it exhibits an irreversible color change upon surpassing a defined threshold temperature.                     <jats:italic>µ</jats:italic>

This approach may be extended to conventional electronic components by integrating a suitable printed thermochromic layer directly onto their surfaces, offering a simple and low-cost method for thermal monitoring, overheat protection and failure prevention. The combination of functional printing with thermochromic detection thus holds promise for applications in quality assurance, safety monitoring, and the development of robust next generation electronics systems.

                  <jats:p>The development of highly efficient and durable dual-functional electrocatalysts for overall water splitting is significant for renewable hydrogen production. abstract: <jats:p>Dielectric capacitors are essential components in pulsed-power and power-electronic systems, but their limited energy density remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, polymorphic polar nanoregions (PNRs) are constructed in lead-free high-entropy (1−x)[0.85(Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-0.15BaTiO3]-xSr(Ta0.6Mg0.3Hf0.1)O3 relaxor ferroelectric ceramics by introducing heterovalent Sr2+, Mg2+, Ta5+, and Hf4+ ions under charge conservation. The increased configurational entropy and local chemical disorder disrupt long-range ferroelectric order, splitting domains into atomic-scale PNRs (&lt;10 nm) and creating a polymorphic R–O–T/C polar network with multiple polarization switching channels. The optimal x = 0.2 ceramic achieves a recoverable energy density of 11.07 J cm−3 with 91.5% efficiency at 588 kV cm−1. It also maintains stable energy storage from 20 to 110 °C and over 106 cycles, and delivers a fast discharge time t0.9 of 104 ns with a power density of 94.8 MW cm−3. This polymorphic PNR strategy provides a promising route for high-performance lead-free capacitive energy storage.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>High-viscosity metallocene poly(α-olefins) are important synthetic lubricant base oils. However, the effects of molecular structure on permanent viscosity loss during mechanical shearing remain insufficiently understood. In this study, mPAO with varying monomer carbon numbers, kinematic viscosities, molecular weight distributions, chain stereoregularities, and residual unsaturation levels were investigated using KRL shear testing, gel permeation chromatography, and spectroscopic characterization. The results showed that the number-average molecular weight decreased and the molecular weight distribution broadened after shearing, whereas the weight-average molecular weight changed only slightly, suggesting that molecular weight changes primarily involved a fraction of the polymer chains. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed oxidation-related changes after shearing, suggesting that oxidation-induced viscosity increase may partially offset shear-induced viscosity loss. Different side-chain structures exhibited distinct shear responses as the monomer carbon number varied. For samples with similar side-chain structures, the viscosity loss rate increased nonlinearly and in a stepwise manner with increasing backbone length. A broader initial molecular weight distribution was associated with greater PVL, whereas higher chain stereoregularity and lower residual unsaturation were associated with improved shear stability. These findings clarify the relationships between molecular structural parameters and the mechanical shear stability of mPAO, providing a basis for designing high-viscosity lubricant base oils with improved shear stability.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To explore the association between different eosinophil counts and short-term acute exacerbations and disease severity in patients with bronchiectasis through a retrospective analysis.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A retrospective study included 438 patients with bronchiectasis. Baseline eosinophil counts were calculated using the first complete blood count upon admission. Patients were divided into three groups based on eosinophil counts (in units of 10
                      <jats:sup>6</jats:sup>
                      cells/L): Group A (eosinophil &lt; 10), Group B (10 ≤ eosinophil &lt; 100), and Group C (eosinophil ≥ 100). We analyzed differences in laboratory parameters, the number of acute exacerbations within one year after discharge across groups. Additionally, we evaluated the exploratory association of eosinophil for acute exacerbations using ROC curves.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      In univariable Cox regression, the HRs of Platelets, Eosinophils and Neutrophils could not be proven to independently predict acute exacerbation in this study, but their potential effects on bronchiectasis outcomes cannot be excluded. In the group of patients with low eosinophil counts, the neutrophil count, CRP, globulin, systemic inflammatory index (SII), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were all significantly higher than those in the other two groups (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.05). Furthermore, this group exhibited a higher incidence of short-term acute exacerbations and a higher frequency of acute exacerbations after discharge. ROC curve indicated that among patients with low eosinophil counts, the combination of eosinophil and neutrophil count demonstrated stronger exploratory association for after-discharge acute exacerbations within one year compared to the overall population, with an AUC of 0.781 for the combined preliminary observation.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Platelets, Eosinophils and Neutrophils’ potential effects on bronchiectasis outcomes cannot be excluded. Low levels of eosinophil counts are somewhat related to the severity of bronchiectasis and short-term acute exacerbations, and can serve as a reference indicator for future research.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>High energy meal plans (HEMP) are increasingly used in paediatric inpatient eating disorder care. This study aimed to determine the impact of HEMP on rate of weight gain, refeeding syndrome (RFS), nasogastric tube (NGT) use and length of stay (LOS), in paediatric eating disorder inpatients with Anorexia Nervosa (AN) or Atypical Anorexia Nervosa (AAN), compared with low energy meal plans (LEMP).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A retrospective pre-post observational study was undertaken on a paediatric ward in Melbourne. Patients with AN or AAN requiring admission under the paediatric eating disorder protocol for nutritional rehabilitation from 15/03/2020–16/03/2023 were included. Patients admitted prior to September 16, 2022, were treated with LEMP (minimum of 1890 kcal/day). Following a change of practice, patients admitted after September 16, 2022, were treated with HEMP (minimum of 2512 kcal/day). Under hospital protocol, patients at significant risk received prophylactic phosphate.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      237 patients commenced treatment on LEMP, and 165 patients on HEMP. Weight gain was faster with HEMP than LEMP (2.17 kg/week (SD 0.930) vs. 1.85 kg/week (SD 1.131);
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.002). HEMP patients were more often classified as being at significant risk of RFS at baseline (58.8% vs. 22.8%;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). Phosphate supplementation was common in both groups and, consistent with baseline risk, more frequent with HEMP (84.2% vs. 63.3%;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001), with similar indications for supplementation and rates of hypophosphatemia between groups. No patients in either group developed RFS. Hypoglycaemia was less common with HEMP (32.1% vs. 47.3%;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.002). There was no significant difference in NGT use (20.6% vs. 15.5%;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.196) or median LOS (HEMP 13 days [IQR 10–16] vs. LEMP 12 days [IQR 8–16];
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.104).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>HEMP was associated with faster weight gain and less hypoglycaemia than LEMP, with no increase in RFS or hypophosphatemia. Prophylactic phosphate supplementation was common in both groups, and its greater use with HEMP likely reflects higher baseline RFS risk rather than energy prescription. LOS did not differ, possibly reflecting differences in illness severity and bed pressures between study periods. These findings support HEMP as a safe and effective approach to refeeding in medically unstable adolescents with AN/AAN when combined with phosphate monitoring.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Organic electrode materials have attracted considerable attention in sodium ion batteries in recent years, yet they still face challenges such as limited energy density, poor cycling stability, and performance degradation under extreme conditions. In this work, a new donor–acceptor (D–A) type monomer, TPA-PTO, based on pyrene-4,5,9,10-tetraone and triphenylamine units is developed, and the pTPA-PTO cathode is successfully constructed through in situ electropolymerization. The pTPA-PTO cathode could successively store Na+ and PF6–, which effectively mitigates concentration polarization and enhances structural stability. Moreover, the electropolymerization further suppresses dissolution and optimizes charge transport. Consequently, pTPA-PTO achieves a high energy density of 697.23 Wh kg–1 at 0.2 A g–1 and demonstrates excellent cycling stability over 1350 cycles. Furthermore, it exhibits long-term durability at 5 A g–1 for 10,000 cycles, with an ultralow capacity decay rate of only 0.0012% per cycle. In addition, the electrode maintains superior performance under high mass loading (7.13 mg cm–2) and across a wide temperature range (–20 to 60 °C). Finally, the pTPA-PTO||HC full cell retains 90% capacity after 2600 cycles at 3 A g–1.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Solar concentrating heating systems with thermal energy storage for supplying thermal power to industrial consumers are becoming increasingly important. Worldwide, dozens of such plants, predominantly parabolic trough systems, are already installed. In Greece and the Republic of Cyprus, two countries with high solar resources, such systems are also installed and operated. This paper presents a review with an analytical description of existing concentrated solar thermal (CST) systems for process heat applications operating at temperatures above 150 °C, with a focus on installations in Greece and Cyprus. For this purpose, a wide range of Internet databases, other sources, and scientific papers were reviewed. Overall, two commercial CST installations and four R&D or demonstration CST projects were identified in Greece and Cyprus. The two operational commercial plants represent a combined installed thermal capacity of 645 kWth. Both commercial installations are based on parabolic trough collector technology and operate at a maximum of 160 °C. Thermal energy storage is integrated only in research and demonstration projects, one of which currently includes large-scale storage. In the research and demonstration sector, CST systems are also being investigated for combined heat, cooling, and electricity generation at operating temperatures up to 400 °C. A comparison of the reviewed CST systems in Greece and Cyprus demonstrates several common trends. Commercial installations to date are generally small- to medium-scale systems focused on industrial heat supply at temperatures below 160 °C. In contrast, research and demonstration projects increasingly target higher operating temperatures of up to 400 °C and integrate advanced concepts such as thermal energy storage and combined cooling, heating, and power generation. The largest CST plant in Greece, which uses PTC technology, produces 5.75 MWth and is installed at the Athenian Brewery in Patras. Parabolic trough collectors dominate most identified installations, while Fresnel collector technology appears mainly in experimental applications. Furthermore, as thermal energy storage is deployed only in research and demonstration-oriented projects, this indicates that storage integration is still at an early stage of commercial deployment in the region. Compared with the Heineken brewery in Seville, Spain, which has a PTC field with a nominal output of 30 MWth, and pressurised-water tank storage with a capacity of 69 MWhth, the installed systems in Greece and Cyprus are small, with the exception of the CST plant installed at the Athenian Brewery. The R&D and demonstration plants cover up to 25% of the thermal energy demand. Only one of the two commercial plants covers 70% of the process thermal demand. Challenges and barriers were identified, and recommendations for overcoming these are given. Trends were identified based on the available data. Because reliable data on the economic performance of the examined projects are lacking, this aspect is not a focus of the paper.</jats:p>

                    Energy consumption forecasting plays a critical role in energy management, grid stability, system reliability, and maintaining the supply–demand balance. In this study, a hybrid long short‐term memory–k‐nearest neighbors (LSTM–KNN) model was developed to estimate an hourly energy consumption using an 80% training 10% validation and 10% testing dataset split. Unlike traditional standalone regressors, the core novelty lies in employing Bayesian‐optimized KNN prior to deep learning as a nonlinear spatial filter. By filtering multivariable noise and selecting key feature subsets, KNN eliminates input dimensionality bottlenecks, allowing the downstream LSTM to focus strictly on modeling complex temporal dependencies without overfitting or computational inefficiency. Model performance was evaluated using mean squared error (MSE), root MSE (RMSE), normalized MSE (NRMSE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), the correlation coefficient (

The models were ranked using a Taylor diagram, and their predictive accuracies were further assessed through regression analysis. Correlation analysis was conducted to investigate the relationships and dependencies among the input variables. Additionally, standard deviations, correlation matrix, and confidence intervals were calculated to evaluate the reliability of the model predictions. The experimental results demonstrated that the hybrid LSTM–KNN model outperformed the compared models in terms of predictive accuracy. The MSE, RMSE, NRMSE, MAPE, and

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Remote northern communities in Canada rely heavily on diesel‐based electricity and heating, resulting in high energy costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and fuel‐supply vulnerabilities. This study develops an integrated techno‐economic framework for the design and evaluation of hybrid multi‐energy systems (HMES) comprising solar photovoltaic (PV), wind turbines, an organic Rankine cycle (ORC)‐based biomass‐fired combined heat and power (BCHP) unit, battery energy storage, and power converters. A multi‐objective optimization approach is employed to minimize the net present cost (NPC) and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), while TOPSIS‐SOMIT‐based multi‐criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is used to rank candidate system configurations. An off‐grid community in a remote northern region of Canada, with an average daily electricity demand of 8,536 kWh, was selected as the case study. The optimal HMES comprises a 450 kW ORC‐BCHP unit, 350 kW of PV capacity, 460 kW of wind capacity, and 2,200 kWh of battery storage, with an initial capital investment of C$13.5 million. The optimized system achieves an LCOE of C$0.458/kWh and an NPC of C$27.1 million. It generates 3,307 MWh of electricity annually, fully meeting community demand while eliminating 821,600 L/year of diesel consumption. Lifecycle CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    emissions decrease from 0.704 to 0.076 kg/kWh, representing an 89% reduction. TOPSIS‐SOMIT‐based MCDA ranks the proposed HMES as the preferred option among seven candidate systems. The results indicate that integrating dispatchable biomass cogeneration with wind, solar, and battery storage can provide a reliable, cost‐effective, and low‐carbon energy solution for remote northern communities.
                  </jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Radiotherapy for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is often limited by intrinsic tumor radioresistance. The clinically approved radiosensitizer sodium glycididazole (CMNa) is restricted by its hypoxia-dependent activity and lack of tumor targeting. Integrin-targeted gold nanoclusters have been extensively investigated as radiosensitizers, yet direct head-to-head comparisons with CMNa are lacking. We synthesized RGDfC-gold nanoclusters (RGDfC-AuNCs) via one-step biomineralization and compared them with CMNa in 4T1 murine TNBC cells and tumor-bearing mice. The nanoclusters showed ultrasmall size, good stability, and exhibited enhanced cellular uptake relative to non-targeted controls. In vitro, radiosensitization performance was assessed by CCK‑8 assays under normoxic and CoCl
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‑mimicked pseudo‑hypoxic conditions. Under equal-total-mass dosing conditions, RGDfC-AuNCs showed superior radiosensitizing trends relative to CMNa across the range of radiation doses tested (2–8 Gy) in both oxygen environments. In 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, RGDfC-AuNCs plus radiotherapy achieved superior tumor growth inhibition (68.29% vs. 50.61%) and a markedly higher sensitization enhancement ratio (2.01 vs. 1.47) compared with CMNa plus radiotherapy, and tumor sections displayed elevated γ-H2AX foci, suggesting enhanced DNA damage. Neither agent induced obvious acute systemic toxicity in hematological, biochemical and histopathological examinations. Collectively, these head‑to‑head observations illustrate the favorable radiosensitization profile of RGDfC‑AuNCs relative to the clinical agent CMNa under the tested conditions, providing a reference for nanocluster-based TNBC radiosensitization.
                  </jats:p>

title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Multi-objective Screening of Hardness and Oxidation Resistance in Refractory High-Entropy Alloys
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical strength and thermal stability, but their practical application is frequently limited by insufficient oxidation resistance. This study develops a machine-learning-assisted workflow for multi-objective screening of hardness and isothermal oxidation resistance in RHEAs. The selected baseline hardness XGBoost model and baseline oxidation random forest model achieve held-out R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    values of 0.79 and 0.76, respectively. The current fitted models screen 109,571 quinary compositions and are compared with six alloys fabricated following an initial ML-assisted multi-objective selection targeting contrasting hardness–oxidation trade-offs. Among these alloys, HHHO_2 exhibits the highest measured hardness of 780 ± 8 HV, whereas LHHO_1 exhibits the lowest specific mass gain of 2.75 ± 0.04 mg/cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , corresponding to an oxidation-resistance index I
                    <jats:sub>ox</jats:sub>
                    of − 0.44 after oxidation at 1000 °C for 20 h. The comparatively large oxidation-prediction errors motivate development of a time-resolved oxidation model incorporating oxidation duration and a composition-weighted Pilling–Bedworth ratio. Within the complete feature set, gradient boosting achieves a five-fold cross-validation R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    of 0.92 ± 0.02 and a held-out R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    of 0.94. For three further alloys selected using the initial advanced-model predictions, the advanced model reduces the mean absolute I
                    <jats:sub>ox</jats:sub>
                    prediction error from 0.46 to 0.21, representing an approximately 53% reduction relative to the baseline oxidation model. The refined HHHO candidate exhibits a hardness of 661 ± 11 HV and a specific mass gain of 6.20 ± 0.01 mg/cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    . Repeated out-of-fold SHAP and cross-model ranking analyses are used to assess the robustness of the learned associations, while multivariate applicability-domain analysis identifies candidates requiring extrapolative interpretation. Overall, the workflow provides an experimentally informed approach for prioritizing RHEA compositions with different hardness–oxidation trade-offs while explicitly accounting for model variability and compositional applicability.
                  </jats:p>

title: Integration of Blockchain Technology Into Smart Grids Through Adaptive Two‐Mode Energy Management With Teletraffic‐Based Admission Control

affiliation.name: Almaty University of Power Engineering and Telecommunications Named After Gumarbek Daukeyev  Almaty Kazakhstan
International Information Technology University  Almaty Kazakhstan

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources has significantly increased the complexity of real‐time energy management in Smart Grid systems, particularly under emergency operating conditions characterised by transmission congestion and temporary power shortages. Smart Grid energy management increasingly requires adaptive mechanisms to handle variable energy demand, limited available resources and network congestion particularly under emergency operating conditions. This paper proposes a dynamic two‐mode energy management architecture that adaptively switches between normal and emergency operating modes by integrating graph‐based generator selection, blockchain‐enabled transaction validation and teletraffic‐based admission control. Under normal operating conditions, energy requests are processed using graph‐based generator selection and blockchain validation. When the system enters an emergency state, an M/M/8 priority queue is activated to regulate the incoming request flow by prioritising critical consumers before graph‐based generator selection is performed. The proposed framework is evaluated on the IEEE 58‐bus power system using comparative simulations against conventional blockchain‐based and graph‐based approaches. The results demonstrate that integrating teletraffic admission control reduces execution time by up to 24.3%, decreases transaction latency by up to 26.5%, increases throughput by up to 48.9% and lowers blockchain gas consumption by approximately 16% while maintaining priority service for critical consumers during congestion.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thiol-ene radical polymerization of CO2-derived lactones containing α,δ-dienes offers a route to sustainable polythioethers with up to 20 wt % CO2. The direct product from CO2/1,3-butadiene telomerization is 3-ethylidene-6-vinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one ((E)EVP) whose α-alkylidene group causes poor reaction kinetics and nonquantitative alkene conversion with dithiols affording low molar mass polythioethers. Here, we use 3,6-divinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (DVP) which was synthesized from the base-catalyzed contrathermodynamic α,β- to β,γ-photodeconjugation of EVP, resulting in the transformation of the α-alkylidene to an α-vinyl functional group. This subtle regio-isomerization was found to result in a 17-fold and 8-fold increase in the rate of α- and δ-ene consumption, respectively, owing to the relative stability of the intermediate carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging these rapid kinetics, high molar mass polythioethers (34 kDa) could be prepared via thiol-ene step-growth polymerization of DVP with 2,2’-(ethylenedioxy)diethanethiol. These molar masses are 10-fold higher than the upper limits obtained with the EVP-derived counterpart, and the polythioethers display mechanical performance suitable as a pressure sensitive adhesive.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>We have demonstrated laser induced fluorescence in a capacitively coupled plasma discharge to measure the most crucial ion properties at a discharge regime suitable for a broad range of plasma research related to plasma processing and dusty plasma investigations that has been impossible for many years. The ion flow measurements in the presence and absence of dust particles show that ions move much faster directionally than expected from thermal motion, with reductions observed in the presence of dust particles. Ion temperatures are also found to exceed room temperature, contrary to a common assumption in the dusty plasma community. These findings represent a significant advancement in experimental plasma research, providing vital information to refine ion-driven process models with insights that span multiple research fields.</jats:p>

title: Child deprivation and parental shielding: a European comparative analysis
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper investigates child material and social deprivation in six large European countries (Germany, Spain, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania) by using four waves of European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions survey (2009, 2014, 2021, and 2024). Relying on the 17 items included in the official child-specific material and social deprivation indicator used at the European level, we provide a systematic cross-country and over-time analysis. We jointly model both the risk of experiencing deprivation and the intensity of child-specific deprivation. Our results indicate that deprived households with children and at least one of the 17 items in deprivation actually encompass two distinct groups: one primarily lacking household items but largely successful in shielding children from the lack of child-specific items, and another experiencing more severe deprivation, characterized by the lack of both household and child-specific items. Deprivation affecting only child-specific items is relatively uncommon. We indirectly test the extent to which parents protect their children from deprivation by showing that households forgo the least severe household-level items before lacking the child-specific items and that individual-level deprivation is more likely in adults than children living with them. The econometric analysis identifies several factors that increase the risk of the more severe form of deprivation, and also documents cross-country heterogeneity, reflecting differences in welfare regimes and broader socio-economic conditions.</jats:p>

title: A Safe and Explainable Bayesian Energy Management Framework with Probabilistic Safety Shielding for EV-Integrated Renewable Microgrids

affiliation.name: Department of Electrical Power Engineering, Durban University of Technology, P.O. Box 1334, Durban 4000, South Africa
Department of Electrical Power Engineering, Durban University of Technology, P.O. Box 1334, Durban 4000, South Africa

abstract: <jats:p>The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and electric vehicle (EV) charging, which is central to the transition towards sustainable energy systems, creates operational challenges for microgrids, where generation uncertainty, demand variability, and charging congestion can lead to energy imbalances and system overloads. This study proposes a Bayesian energy management framework integrating probabilistic forecasting, explainable charging-decision modelling, and safety-constrained action filtering for renewable microgrids with EV charging. The framework combines Bayesian Ridge regression for demand forecasting, Gaussian Process regression for photovoltaic (PV) generation forecasting, Bayesian charging classification, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and an independent Safety Shield to assess the operational feasibility of candidate charging decisions. On an independent test set of 150 observations, the demand forecasting model achieved an R2 of 0.8546 and 90.00% empirical coverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals. The charging classifier attained 98.00% agreement with reference decisions and a Brier score of 0.0132. However, the unshielded controller recorded 139 overload events, corresponding to an observed overload rate of 92.67% (95% confidence interval: 87.35–95.86%). With the Safety Shield enabled, no overload events were observed in the test set, yielding an observed rate of 0% (95% confidence interval: 0–2.50%). This reduction was accompanied by a decrease in decision agreement to 64.00% and reported EV charging curtailment of 1567.33 kWh, illustrating the operational trade-off between overload avoidance and charging availability. Both shielded and unshielded configurations reported a daily operating cost of $210.44, compared with $ 476.73 for the rule-based benchmark, equivalent to an approximately 55.86% reduction based on the reported costs. However, this economic comparison excludes the cost of curtailed EV charging, and the absence of observed overloads does not establish zero population-level risk. Overall, the results demonstrate that high charging-decision agreement alone is insufficient to ensure physical feasibility and support the integration of explicit safety filtering with uncertainty-aware prediction and interpretable decision-making for the safe and sustainable operation of EV-integrated renewable microgrids.</jats:p>

title: Macrophage ferroptosis in atherosclerosis: unraveling novel antiatherogenic targets and pharmacological strategies
abstract: <jats:p>Atherosclerosis is the underlying cause of many cardiovascular diseases, and macrophages play a pivotal role in its intricate landscape, significantly regulating inflammation, lipid metabolism, and iron metabolism. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, and its process is related to macrophage function in atherosclerosis. During atherosclerosis, macrophages contribute to the removal of harmful substances such as lipids and inhibit early development. However, macrophage ferroptosis promotes inflammatory progression, facilitates foam cell and necrotic core formation, promotes calcification, and increases plaque instability. This review first summarizes macrophage heterogeneity in atherosclerosis, then integrates their roles in lipid handling and iron metabolism, and finally focuses on how ferroptosis shapes plaque inflammation, necrotic core formation, calcification, and instability. Currently, the pharmacologic treatment of atherosclerosis is based on lipid-lowering agents, but it remains deficient. Therefore, this review encompasses a variety of potential pharmacological treatments, including organic compounds, natural plant extracts and derivatives, and compound formulations, which can inhibit macrophage ferroptosis and may constitute a novel approach for atherosclerosis treatment. Taken together, this review provides a breakthrough strategy for treating atherosclerosis and establishes a navigational pathway for future therapeutic interventions by targeting macrophage ferroptosis.</jats:p>

title: When Does Nanosizing Matter for Radiation Shielding? A Physical Bound, a Test of Reported Nano Advantages and Grain-Size Rules for Glass Gamma–Neutron Shields

affiliation.name: Department of Chemistry and Chemical Processing Technologies, Çaycuma Food and Agriculture Vocational School, Zonguldak Bülent Ecevit University, 67900 Zonguldak, Türkiye

abstract: <jats:p>Nano-sized fillers are widely reported to attenuate gamma rays better than micro-sized fillers of the same composition, yet it is unclear when particle size can matter at all. At fixed composition and density, Jensen’s inequality makes the homogeneous mixture an upper bound on narrow-beam attenuation, so nanosizing can only remove a heterogeneity penalty. We show that this penalty collapses onto a master curve in the optical size τ=Δμd and derive a packing correction from the Percus–Yevick structure factor that agrees with equilibrated Monte Carlo packings within about 4%. Without fitting, explicit packings reproduce a 37 vol% B4C self-shielding benchmark to within 1.2–3.4% for four cross-section sets, although no measurement uncertainties are available for it. For polydisperse powders the volume-weighted diameter D[4,3] is the appropriate size measure, whereas the number mean can misstate the loss by up to 76% for geometric standard deviations up to 2. In broad-beam geometry the grain effect shrinks by 15–63%, depending on slab thickness and energy, above absorption edges mainly through K fluorescence. We then compiled 65 published nano/micro studies and tested those with paired data against bounds computed for their own compositions. Above 500 keV, where no physical mechanism permits an excess, the nano samples of all 26 studies with paired data exceed the bound by a median of 9.6%, and those of the 22 studies that pass a set-up check by 8.9%, whereas matched micro samples agree with it. This excess cannot arise from grain physics or from an error in filler fraction. Its energy independence is consistent with, but does not prove, a multiplicative measurement error that affects the nano samples. All but one of the studies that show it in a testable form belong to one network of co-authoring groups, and the single independent study shows a smaller excess of about 5%. For glass-matrix gamma–neutron shields at the loadings and loss criteria considered, only the thermal-neutron absorber requires fine grains, about 0.5 µm for Gd2O3 and 5–10 µm for B4C, whereas the gamma filler can remain micrometer-sized. These results show when nanosizing is worth its cost and motivate a minimal reporting standard for attenuation studies.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Commercial human spaceflight is broadening access to in-orbit research and enabling a wider range of organizations to evaluate technologies in crewed space environments. For soft radiation shielding, this creates a validation challenge because folding, compression, stowage, deployment and human interaction can modify the physical configuration that governs radiation response. We propose that physical configuration forms part of the shielding state and that its evolution through the mission lifecycle should be preserved in the validation record. The TEXRAD experiment, conducted during Axiom Mission 3 on the International Space Station, provides a crewed-mission case for this approach. Dosimeters travelling with the flight samples associated the flight configuration with its local radiation environment, while pre- and post-exposure characterization documented the material response. Parallel sample histories provided reference conditions needed to interpret the response of the flight samples. From this case, we derive a system-level framework based on configuration traceability, interpretability and validation continuity. The framework links shielding state, exposure and measured response along a progressive validation pathway, from controlled material testing and passive orbital exposure to crew-handled configurations and integrated shielding systems. This approach provides a transferable basis for generating interpretable evidence as soft radiation-shielding technologies progress toward sustained human spaceflight.</jats:p>

title: Immune cell-resolved genetic associations nominate FADS1 as a candidate locus in metabolic syndrome
abstract:
<jats:p>Aim: To identify immune-cell-resolved genetic associations with metabolic syndrome (MetS) and prioritize candidate loci for further investigation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Methods: We integrated cis-expression quantitative trait loci from 14 peripheral immune-cell populations with genome-wide association study summary statistics for two aggregate metabolic phenotypes and five component traits. We combined Mendelian randomization (MR), Bayesian colocalization, and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) with heterogeneity in dependent instruments (HEIDI) testing. Transcriptomic and cross-sectional population analyses provided additional biological context.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Results: Among 42,257 primary MR tests, 3,141 gene-cell-trait associations met the prespecified false-discovery-rate threshold after outcome-specific correction. In a sensitivity analysis applying Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all 42,257 tests, 2,950 associations remained significant. Formal Bayesian colocalization supported 159 associations involving 68 genes. A broader exploratory pool contained 439 associations involving 192 genes, including 280 associations retained through a linkage disequilibrium (LD)-based screening criterion without formal colocalization support. Fatty acid desaturase 1 (FADS1) was prioritized as a candidate at the fatty acid desaturase (FADS) locus, which is associated with polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism. Genetically proxied FADS1 expression and the serum log-transformed ratio of arachidonic acid (AA) to dihomo-γ-linolenic acid (DGLA) showed differing metabolic association patterns; the AA/DGLA ratio represents an indirect and non-gene-specific biochemical proxy rather than a direct measure of FADS1 activity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Conclusion: Immune-cell-resolved genetic analyses nominate the FADS locus and FADS1 as candidates for further investigation, but do not establish the effector gene, mediating cell type, or lipid-remodeling mechanism. Direct functional and lipid measurements are needed to test these hypotheses.</jats:p>

title: High-Entropy Alloys, Carbides, and Oxides for Lead-Free Radiation Shielding: A Critical Review

affiliation.name: Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering and Information Technology, Onaizah Colleges, Qassim 56447, Saudi Arabia

abstract: <jats:p>High-entropy materials, which combine four or more principal elements in one phase, can hold high-atomic-number species for photon attenuation, strong neutron absorbers, and light or load-bearing elements in a single, chemically stable solid, which makes them candidates for multifunctional radiation shields. This review examines high-entropy alloys, carbides, and oxides as radiation-attenuating media, a role distinct from irradiation tolerance and not previously consolidated, and benchmarks them against lead and lead-free incumbents, separating computed from measured values. Between about 1 and 4 MeV, the mass attenuation coefficient varies little with composition, hydrogen apart, so density governs per-thickness performance and matching lead needs about 12 g cm−3; at 0.1–0.2 MeV diluted refractory chemistries need 18–22 g cm−3. The only fabricated tungsten-bearing alloy that states its density, Ta-Ti-V-W at 11.63 g cm−3, reaches 96% of lead’s linear attenuation at 1.25 MeV and 85% at 0.662 MeV, below tungsten, its heavy alloys, and tungsten carbide. High-entropy oxide fillers do not out-attenuate Bi2O3 per unit mass but combine photon attenuation with gadolinium capture in one phase. Of 39 studies, 21 measure attenuation, one measures lead in the same setup, and none measures charged-particle shielding. The review contributes a minimum reporting standard, a composition-level design framework, and a data-driven design workflow.</jats:p>

Thermally programmable metamaterials via bimaterial beam architectures
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thermoresponsive metamaterials offer a powerful route to adaptive mechanical systems, but broad and reversible thermal programming of force-displacement behavior and multistability has remained elusive. Here, we introduce a general design paradigm for thermally programmable multistable metastructures based on bimaterial beam cells that harness coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch to reconfigure mechanical states. The unit cells are engineered to undergo thermally triggered transitions between monostable and bistable regimes, enabling direct control of local stability and snap-through behavior. Hierarchical assembly of these cells with designed thickness gradients translates this cell-level tunability into system-level programmability, yielding metastructures with temperature-controlled mechanical responses, deformation sequences, and energy landscapes. A predictive theoretical framework captures the thermomechanical response across operating conditions and agrees with experiments. We demonstrate precise thermal tuning of multistability and energy absorption, and further showcase programmed mechanical information encoding and temperature-dependent decryption as representative functionalities. This strategy expands the design space of programmable metamaterials and establishes a scalable platform for adaptive soft robotics, shape-morphing architectures, flexible electronics, and reconfigurable impact-mitigation systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Guided Selection of Extraction Conditions for Fruit and Medicinal Plant By-Products: Target Compound Content and Relative Composition as Decision Criteria

affiliation.name: Independent Researcher, Seoul 06300, Republic of Korea

abstract: <jats:p>Stricter composition screening can prevent unsuitable extraction recommendations while withholding suitable ones. This retrospective benchmark evaluated target compound content and relative composition as decision criteria, comparing selection by predicted target content alone with additional predicted-share screening, using identical predictions and held-out candidates within datasets. The collection comprised 39 datasets from 28 studies, with extensions analyzed separately. Success required measured target content and share within the analytical panel to meet training-derived thresholds. Across seven primary fruit by-product datasets and five focal models, screening increased attainment in 3 of 35 comparisons, by at most 1.4 percentage points, under the original fitting settings, common evaluation sets, and 60th-percentile content and median share thresholds. In grape pomace, reduced quadratic regression gained eight successes but lost 60, including 45 through additional abstention. Saffron floral residues and sage herbal dust provided separate medicinal plant evidence with source-specific limitations. Matched refits and threshold analyses showed that recommendations and some rule comparisons depended on the settings. Assessing compliance with ingredient specifications requires prospective validation across independent material batches using measurements on the relevant product basis. The benchmark supports choosing selection rules by jointly evaluating attainment, unsuitable recommendations, and abstention under specified analytical panels, chemical requirements, and cost assumptions.</jats:p>

title: The Inpatient Blood-Pressure Paradox: Molecular Pathology of Adaptive Hypertension, Silent Target-Organ Injury and Iatrogenic Harm
abstract: <jats:p>Elevated blood pressure (BP) is common during non-cardiovascular hospitalisation, yet the biological meaning of transient inpatient BP elevation remains uncertain. Asymptomatic elevated inpatient BP is exceptionally common, having been reported in approximately 50%–72% of hospitalisations, while markedly elevated asymptomatic inpatient BP has been documented in approximately 10% of adults admitted for conditions other than hypertension [1]. The clinical scale of the problem therefore contrasts sharply with the relative absence of evidence defining when an inpatient BP elevation represents biological injury rather than contextual physiological stress.Current practice distinguishes hypertensive emergency, in which acute hypertension-mediated target-organ damage is demonstrable, from asymptomatic BP elevation, in which such injury is clinically absent. This binary framework may be biologically incomplete because acute stressors can substantially raise BP, conventional tests may miss early cellular injury, and rapid pharmacological BP reduction may itself disturb renal, coronary or cerebral autoregulation. This technical report proposes a molecular-pathology framework that treats inpatient hypertension as a dynamic interaction among pressure burden, physiological context, cellular injury and treatment response. The framework integrates tissue-of-origin cell-free DNA, including endothelial NOS3 methylation signatures, kidney-specific methylation markers and cardiomyocyte-associated methylation signatures, with urinary cellcycle-arrest biomarkers, conventional renal and cardiac indices, endothelial glycocalyx-shedding markers, endothelial extracellular vesicles and copeptin. Serial sampling before and after antihypertensive exposure is proposed to distinguish stress-dominant or potentially adaptive BP elevation from molecularly silent target-organ injury and treatment-associated tissue damage. Pressure-time burden, BP variability, rate of BP reduction and deviation from premorbid BP are incorporated rather than relying on isolated thresholds. The framework is intended for prospective multicentre validation and subsequent phenotype-stratified randomised trials, not immediate biomarker-directed treatment. If validated, molecular phenotyping could help shift inpatient BP management from treatment of a numerical threshold towards treatment of the biological process represented by that pressure.</jats:p>

title: Radiographic Evaluation of the Proximity between Mandibular Molar Roots and the Inferior Alveolar Nerve Canal Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) Among Different Age Groups in Najaf City: A Cross-Sectional Study

affiliation.name: BDS, MSC, Department of Oral Diagnosis, University of Kufa, Najaf, Iraq

journal: International Journal of Medical Science and Dental Health
abstract:
<jats:p>Aims: This study aimed to evaluate the proximity between mandibular molars roots and the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) canal across different age and sex groups using Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) imaging modality in Najaf city.

Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on CBCT scans of 90 patients, aged 18-80 years. Patients were categorized into three age groups: 18-30, 31-45, 45-80 years. The shortest distance between the roots of the first, second, and third mandibular molars and the IAN canal was measured bilaterally using specialized CBCT software. Statistical analysis was performed to assess variations between age groups, sex groups, and sides of the mandible.

Results: The mean distance between the mandibular molar roots and the IAN canal was significantly smaller in the third molars compared to the first molars. Age-related differences were observed, with younger patients showing the smallest mean distances; this was statistically significant. No significant differences were found between the right and left sides. Gender differences were minimal.

Conclusion: CBCT imaging was effective in evaluating the relationship between mandibular molar roots and the inferior alveolar nerve canal. The results showed that the distance between molar roots and the canal generally increased with age

and was slightly greater in males than in females. No significant difference was observed between the right and left sides of the mandible. In addition, the distance decreased from the first molar to the third molar, with the third molar showing the closest proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve canal. These findings highlight the importance of careful radiographic evaluation before performing surgical or endodontic procedures in the mandibular molar region.</jats:p>

title: Advances in prediction of drug-target thermodynamics and kinetics: from molecular simulations to artificial intelligence

abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In the drug discovery field, drug affinity has long been considered the gold standard for designing small compounds with therapeutic activity. However, since the beginning of the 21st century, kinetic parameters, which are directly related to compound efficacy, have increasingly been recognized as central to the rational design of new drugs. However, such data are scarce, while the experimental determination of the association and dissociation rate constants,
                    <jats:italic>k</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>on</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>k</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>off</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    , is costly and time-consuming. Molecular simulations, such as Molecular Dynamics (MD) calculations have been proposed to predict those kinetic constants, despite known limitations. With the rapid development of AI-based tools, researchers are now proposing advanced methodologies that leverage both data-driven learning from existing datasets and physics-based modelling through MD simulations. This review presents a critical overview of MD-based approaches for estimating protein-ligand binding free energies and rate constants. It then examines data-driven prediction methods and ML-assisted molecular simulations, with particular attention to validation and current limitations. Finally, it discusses the crucial need for new data with respect to the FAIR principles and methodological developments needed to further improve prediction quality.
